Five arrested after suspicious vehicles near RAF Fairford
United Kingdom
Unknown Publisher

14:01:27 BST
22:01:27 KST

A major incident has been declared near RAF Fairford after five men were arrested on suspicion of offences under the Explosives Act, with around 85 households evacuated while Army bomb disposal specialists examine three suspicious vehicles.
Gloucestershire Constabulary said officers were called at around 12.45am on Sunday 27 September following a report of three suspicious vehicles travelling towards RAF Fairford. Armed officers responded and subsequently arrested five men in the Whelford area, all of whom remain in police custody.
In an update issued at around 1.55pm, police said: “At around 12.45am today, Sunday the 27th of September, police received a call relating to three suspicious vehicles travelling towards RAF Fairford. Armed officers responded, and subsequently arrested five men in the Whelford area on suspicion of committing offences under the Explosives Act. The men were taken into custody, where they remain.”
A 400-metre cordon has been established around the vehicles while an Army explosive ordnance disposal team examines them. Around 85 households have been advised to leave their homes as a precaution, with a nearby leisure centre opened for residents unable to stay with family or friends.
Police said: “A 400 metre cordon has been put in place around the vehicles while the Army’s explosive ordnance disposal unit examine them. As a precaution, around 85 households have been advised to evacuate while these examinations take place. A nearby leisure centre has been opened for those who are unable to stay with family or friends.”
The force said work was continuing to establish the full nature of the incident and confirmed that officers were in contact with partner organisations at both local and national level, including counter-terrorism policing.
The update continued: “The emergency services have well-rehearsed plans for dealing with major incidents such as this. Work to establish the full nature of this incident is ongoing, and we are in constant communication with our partners, both locally and nationally. In particular, we are working closely with our partners in counter-terrorism policing.”
Gloucestershire Constabulary said its immediate focus remained on the local community and thanked those who had been required to leave their homes.
Police said: “Gloucestershire Police’s focus at this time is on the local community, and I’d like to thank the residents who have left their homes this morning for their understanding and support. We appreciate the disruption that this will have caused to both them and other local residents in the area, and we’d like to reassure them that we are working as quickly as we can to get them back into their properties.”
The force also urged people not to speculate about the circumstances surrounding the incident while enquiries continue, saying: “We would also please ask the public not to speculate, but to follow official channels for all updates.”
An earlier police statement said a number of properties in the Whelford area were being evacuated following the declaration of the major incident.
The force said: “A number of properties are currently being evacuated in the Whelford area following the declaration of a major incident.
“It follows the arrest of several men on suspicion of offences under the Explosives Act.
“The Army’s specialist explosive ordnance disposal team are currently examining a number of vehicles.
“The local residents are being evacuated to a nearby leisure centre.
“A cordon is currently in place but we’d like to reassure people that we believe this incident is contained.
“We are working closely with our partners and are enacting the well-rehearsed plans we have in place.”
RAF Fairford is a US Air Force-operated base in Gloucestershire used by the 501st Combat Support Wing and frequently supports deployments of American military aircraft to the UK. Police have not said that the five men, the vehicles or the alleged explosives offences are connected to activity at the airbase beyond stating that the vehicles were reported travelling towards RAF Fairford.
Separate social media reports published before the police announcement claimed force protection measures at Fairford had been increased, including claims that the base had moved to Force Protection Condition Delta.
A US Air Force spokesperson, responding to reporting about security at Fairford, said: “We are aware of the current reporting. For operational security reasons we will not discuss specific force protection measures.”
Force Protection Conditions are used by the US military to set security measures according to the assessed threat. Delta is the highest level and is normally associated with a terrorist attack having occurred or intelligence indicating an imminent threat at a specific location, but the US Air Force has not confirmed that Fairford is operating at that level.

Probiotic bacteria might offer a temporary boost for sleep and vitality in mild depression
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-27
13:00:28 UTC
22:00:28 KST

Taking a daily probiotic supplement may temporarily improve sleep and vitality in people experiencing mild to moderate depression. Over an eight-week period, a specific bacterial strain offered rapid boosts to mental well-being, though the initial advantages leveled out as time went on. The findings were published in Experimental and Clinical Psychopharmacology.
Mood disorders are a leading cause of disability worldwide. People experiencing mild to moderate depressive symptoms are often managed in primary care medical settings rather than by specialized psychiatrists. Many of these individuals hesitate to start traditional antidepressant medications due to concerns that the side effects might outweigh the modest clinical benefits.
The human digestive tract hosts trillions of microorganisms that help digest food and regulate the immune system. These microbes also produce chemicals that communicate directly with the brain through a network called the gut-brain axis. For instance, certain gut bacteria manufacture precursors to serotonin, a chemical messenger that stabilizes mood. When the microbial balance in the digestive tract is disrupted, it can negatively influence mental health and physiological stress responses.
Researchers are exploring psychobiotics as an alternative or supplementary option for mood management. Psychobiotics are live bacteria that provide mental health benefits when ingested. A team led by Kelly M. Seamans, a researcher at the biotechnology company Novonesis in Ireland, wanted to see if a specific strain could relieve low mood. The strain, known as Bifidobacterium longum 1714, had previously shown promise in earlier trials for improving sleep quality and softening the biological response to stress.
The researchers designed a trial involving 168 adults between the ages of 18 and 70. All participants had mild to moderate depressive symptoms, which the team confirmed using standard psychological checklists. To isolate the effects of the bacteria, participants were excluded if they were currently taking antidepressants, sleep medications, or undergoing cognitive behavioral therapy.
The participants were randomly divided into two equal groups. One group took two capsules a day containing the active Bifidobacterium longum 1714 strain. The other group received identical placebo capsules containing inactive ingredients like corn starch.
Neither the researchers nor the participants knew who received the active supplement or the placebo until the trial concluded. This double-blind design helps prevent expectations from skewing the final results. The intervention lasted for eight weeks, with researchers evaluating the participants at the midpoint and the end.
The primary goal was to measure changes in overall depression severity. To do this, the researchers used the Beck Depression Inventory. This is a standard survey that asks participants to rate symptoms like sadness and loss of interest over the previous two weeks.
By the end of the eight weeks, both groups reported feeling substantially better than they did at the start of the study. The difference in overall depression scores between the probiotic group and the placebo group was not statistically significant at any point in the trial. The active bacteria did not provide a unique advantage for this primary mood metric.
While the primary mood scores did not diverge between the two groups, the researchers noted other changes during the first four weeks. At the trial’s midpoint, participants taking the probiotic experienced a greater decrease in a secondary survey of depressive symptoms compared to the placebo group. The probiotic group also reported much better sleep quality.
The sleep evaluations assessed factors like how long it takes to fall asleep and how often a person wakes up during the night. By week four, the probiotic group had shorter sleep latency, meaning they fell asleep faster than the control group. The total number of people classified as poor sleepers also dropped more sharply in the group taking the bacteria.
The probiotic group also reported higher scores in specific quality-of-life categories at week four. These categories included mental health, social role functioning, and vitality. Vitality refers to a person’s physical and mental energy levels, which often plummet during depressive episodes.
By the end of the eight-week study, most of these early advantages faded. The placebo group experienced continued improvements, effectively catching up to the probiotic group in sleep quality and most mood categories. The differences between the groups at week eight were not statistically significant for almost all measurements.
There was one exception to this convergence at the end of the trial. The probiotic group retained a measurable edge in self-reported vitality scores at week eight. The researchers noted that higher vitality scores correlated closely with lower overall depression scores across the study.
Throughout the study, the researchers monitored participants for adverse effects by conducting blood tests and checking vital signs. The probiotic was deemed safe, and there were no prominent differences in side effects between the active and placebo groups. Most reported health issues, such as minor gastrointestinal complaints, were typical for dietary supplements.
The strong response in the placebo group limits the ability to draw firm conclusions about the probiotic’s long-term effectiveness. In clinical trials for mild depression, participants often improve simply because they expect the treatment to work or because they are receiving regular attention from health professionals. It is possible that the bacteria provide a rapid initial benefit that is eventually matched by the natural course of healing and the placebo effect.
The study design also left a few lifestyle variables unmonitored. While the researchers recorded dietary and exercise habits at the beginning of the trial, they did not track these behaviors throughout the eight weeks. Unmeasured changes in a participant’s daily routine, such as exercising more frequently, could have influenced their mood and sleep.
The participant pool was also predominantly female. Hormonal fluctuations can heavily influence mood and energy levels, but the researchers did not track menstrual cycles or hormone therapy. Future trials could control for these variables by focusing on specific demographic groups or tracking biological markers more closely.
The study, “Effects of Bifidobacterium longum 1714 on Low Mood and Related Symptoms: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Trial,” was authored by Kelly M. Seamans, Elaine Patterson, Caterina Holz, David Groeger, Jouni Junnila, Fergus Collins, Eileen F. Murphy, Katy Sorensen, and Timothy G. Dinan.

Mass publication of data on deceased persons makes historians' work easier
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-27
13:00:00 UTC
22:00:00 KST

Mass publication of data on deceased persons makes historians' work easier
In September, the Ministry of the Interior began publishing, as open data, the names, birth and death dates, and personal identification codes of deceased persons. For historians and name researchers, machine‑readable data makes research easier.
Enel Pungas, head of the population operations department at the Ministry of the Interior, explained that publishing the data is important, for example, for institutions with which the deceased had contracts. "All institutions need this information that a person has died," she said.
Historian and name researcher Fred Puss said that in many countries data about deceased persons has been public for decades. According to Puss, the data is also important for historians, and searching for it across different registers has been difficult — especially concerning people who died between 1944 and 1957.
A name researcher can learn from this data, for example, when a particular surname in Estonia died out — meaning when the last bearer of that name passed away.
"Unfortunately, this happens constantly. Forty‑four percent of all Estonian surnames are represented by only one bearer, and when that one bearer dies, the name disappears from Estonia. A large part of those names are not of Estonian origin, but among them are also Estonian names," Puss said.
The Data Protection Inspectorate asked the Ministry of the Interior to assess, before publishing the names, whether making them public could cause discomfort to the relatives of the deceased.
"In the Estonian Personal Data Protection Act there is even a provision that allows certain personal data of deceased persons to be processed without consent, but if such data is processed more broadly as open data, then in fact an additional impact assessment should be carried out," said Geili Keppi, a lawyer at the Data Protection Inspectorate.
Pungas said that as a result of the impact assessment, the data of the deceased will not be published immediately, but seven days after death. The Statistics Office and the Estonian Institute for Health Development have also reviewed the level of detail in death‑cause statistics to ensure that no one can be identified by cause of death.
--
Editor: Valner Väino, Argo Ideon

Investigation reveals Iranian-linked social media accounts posing as Israelis ahead of elections
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-27
12:59:31 UTC
21:59:31 KST

Iranian-linked actors have been linked to a series of social media accounts posing as Israeli citizens, where they are posting allegations about the upcoming election, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, and divisive issues such as the haredi (ultra-Orthodox) draft, according to a new open-source intelligence investigation published by Golden Owl.
AI-powered open-source intelligence platform Golden Owl published its investigation on Thursday, which mapped what appears to be an Iranian-linked interference campaign in a two-phase investigation conducted between August 22 and September 22. Researchers analyzed 21,533 posts and flagged 1,516 for anomalies, including election misinformation, foreign framing, and anomalous account identities or behavior.
Despite voting not opening until October 27, multiple accounts were found to have published preemptive claims that the election result would be stolen, while several others published false information about the vote itself.
Accounts based outside Israel posted claims in Arabic, Russian, and English across major social media platforms that the election would be postponed or suspended due to foreign interference, with taxes and mortgage payments frozen alongside the postponement.
Spike in electoral fraud claims
Claims of electoral fraud spiked on September 9, after Likud alleged that former Fatah official Mohammed Dahlan was behind a Haaretz report claiming that UAE President Mohamed bin Zayed had personally warned Netanyahu of an impending major Hamas operation before October 7, 2023, and again on September 17, around the time of a Supreme Court ruling banning parties from transmitting real-time voter data on election day.
A claim that “the upcoming Israeli elections of 27 October will be postponed by a month and a week” was reposted four times within minutes on September 20 after being posted by Yemen-based @BRany4443. @Tamam3o, @Mustapha69ma and newly created US-based @GentileQueennie also claimed the election date had been moved to October 26.
The first phase identified 237 accounts as suspicious actors and 57 as part of a foreign influence campaign.
The research also found that dark-web sellers were offering services and datasets targeting Israel, including Telegram accounts registered to Israeli phone numbers and sold in bulk as ready-to-use sessions.
Social media marketing panel SMMTG.PRO and similar services were also found to be selling Telegram subscribers, boosts, votes, and views in more than 20 countries, including subscribers targeting Israeli audiences.
Other listings included a database titled “Database elector.co.il,” the domain of the voter-management app used by Likud, on the DarkNetArmy forum, as well as advertisements for datasets including a “Facebook database of four million Israelis,” “Israel government phone numbers” and Israeli election data from 2020 and 2021.
Golden Owl’s investigation also identified a layered infrastructure linked to Iran that it said sought to manipulate the Israeli public. After mapping 119,717 accounts and 294,980 relationships, researchers identified coordinated personas embedded in conversations among real Israeli voters, using patriotic imagery, carefully designed language, and genuine political grievances to present themselves as Israeli women, reservists, secular voters, or religious activists.
The account @YaaraShalev, which was also cited in a March 2026 situation report by the Diaspora Ministry as an example of “persona-based engagement” in Iran’s Hebrew-language influence campaign, presents itself as being run by a Jewish Israeli woman focused on democracy and peace.
However, the account, first created in 2012, had its username changed in July 2025 and immediately began posting videos about politics daily. Though the account is listed as North American, records show that the X/Twitter account is accessed through a West Asian build of the Android app.
After conducting a background check across multiple social media platforms, Golden Owl found that the persona’s identity appeared to have been assembled using borrowed and synthetic images.
The photographs attached to “Yaara” across different platforms were inconsistent, with some traceable to publicly circulated images of an adult-film performer and others flagged as AI-generated.
Golden Owl found that the Yaara account serves as the content hub for the network. It also contains the most-viewed post among those analyzed, gaining 688,434 views on a post calling for mass emigration from Israel.
The words and narratives published in Yaara’s posts were also regularly copied from other parts of the network. Of the 40 posts collected by researchers from @kig_voice, a Hebrew-language channel previously identified in a government assessment as part of an Iranian influence campaign, 35% later resurfaced as captions or opening lines in posts from “Yaara.”
The research also identified @miriamkozak, which has nearly 19,000 followers, as the operation’s audience node and found an anomalous pattern of self-amplification.
Though the Miriam account claims to be based in Israel, X records it as being based in Europe and shows it connecting through a European Android build. The Israeli watchdog FakeReporter also exposed it as fictitious in January 2024, after it posted an AI-generated image of Netanyahu that genuine Israeli politicians then circulated as evidence of left-wing incitement.
During the 2022 election, the Miriam account pushed claims of Arab electoral fraud and anti-left messaging before switching to intense anti-Netanyahu content.
In 2025, it created a Facebook group “supporting” MK Naama Lazimi that drew roughly 8,000 genuine Israeli members before Meta removed it following a press inquiry.
Neither the “Yaara” nor the “Miriam” account responded to The Jerusalem Post’s request for comment.
Four other Israeli personas, @Raamihadad1985, @Ivandray50, @tlmqr1990 and @mardeankabooti, were also flagged by X’s transparency panel as accessing the platform through the “Iran Android App.” All four accounts present themselves as Israeli and post in Hebrew about the election, while X locates them to Germany or Finland. Golden Owl said this suggested that the accounts could be operating from inside Iran using a European VPN or proxies.
Additional evidence emerged in the case of @mardeankabooti. The handle is the Persian word for “Spider-Man.” The account was created in 2019 and, until April 2026, posted exclusively in Persian, arguing with other Iranian users about Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and Iranian politics.
On August 26, 2026, it re-emerged as “Alon Strauss,” with an Israeli flag as its avatar, posting Hebrew hashtags for The Democrats and Yair Golan and calling Netanyahu “the most disgusting animal in nature.”
“This is an Iranian user’s account, rebranded as an Israeli voice nine weeks before the election,” Golden Owl concluded.
Many of the accounts connected to the personas also claim to be Israeli, though X places them in countries where there is unlikely to be a Diaspora community. The account @AviLevi67, which has changed its handle three times, is based in Egypt, as are @RonenMichil, @ytn82922 and @YuvalYitzhk5p2k. Similarly, @AmitCigen96 and @mws1499826 are, according to X data, based in Yemen.
Many accounts created months before the election
INFLUENCE OPERATIONS need accounts, and accounts created for an election tend to be created shortly before it. Of the 32 classified personas connected to the seeds, 26, or 81%, were created in 2025 or 2026, including 19 in 2026.
Some previously dormant American accounts were also reactivated years after they went cold and began posting in Hebrew, as was the case with @Ayelet_Goren_.
The accounts also often repeat the same claims. On August 26, @Malishalev posted in Hebrew, “The Iranians have already put him and his family in their sights for assassination. If he is reelected, Israel may pay a very heavy price to protect him and his family and save their lives.” The same post was made by @E_katrina_s on August 31.
The two accounts that published the aforementioned text were notably renamed 11 minutes apart and share nine additional repeated texts.
The repeated posts across the multiple personas share common themes, with the central claim being that Netanyahu is personally responsible for October 7.
The accounts also repeat claims framing the Qatargate scandal as proof that Netanyahu sold Israel for money, that Netanyahu is allowing draft-dodging haredim to hold a powerful role in society, that Netanyahu will either rig the election or start a new war, and that emigrating from Israel is the most rational option and Israelis should refuse to join the military.
Though few of the persona accounts have a large following, Golden Owl said that this was a deliberate design rather than a weakness in the influence campaign. The Golden Owl said the collective aim relies on placement, repetition, and borrowed amplification, allowing the messages to reach audiences far larger than the accounts’ own followings.
In the month before publication, content from the persona network was displayed roughly one million times and generated 9,112 measured interactions, rising to around 27,475 over the full analysis window. Golden Owl estimated that 4,100 to 12,400 distinct accounts engaged with the network, including 362 identified by name. Of those, 76% are based in Israel.
Those Israeli accounts helped amplify messages from the foreign-operated personas to their own followers, potentially extending their reach well beyond their direct audiences.

Survey reveals substantial acceptance of September 11 conspiracy theories blaming CIA, Zionists
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-27
12:59:18 UTC
21:59:18 KST

There has been substantial acceptance of 9/11 conspiracy theories, and many people blame the CIA or Zionists for the terrorist attacks, according to a new survey released on Sunday by the Jerusalem Center for Security and Foreign Affairs (JCFA)
Titled “Twenty-Five Years After 9/11: Conspiracy Theories Challenge Historical Fact,” the study was conducted by JCFA senior researcher Dr. Irwin J. Mansdorf and International Freedom Coalition president Dr. Charles Jacobs.
The research examined shifting public perceptions 25 years after the 2001 attacks. The data for the study was collected this September 10-16.
There were substantial differences across religious, generational, and partisan groups in beliefs about 9/11, national-security threats, and US institutions, the report said.
The survey outlined key takeaways from an analysis of 416 Muslim American respondents, 429 isolated non-Muslim respondents, and broader generational and partisan cohorts, which included a general population cohort of 513 respondents, among them 24 individuals who identified as Muslim.
One-third of American Muslims neutral on government-mandated 9/11 curriculum
The data documented a “severe disintegration of a shared American reality, operating across two major vectors: a profound socio-religious chasm and a sweeping decay of historical factuality within the general public,” the report said.
JCFA tracked public opinion across these populations to examine how religious affiliation, political orientation, and age influence understanding of the attacks.
The widest reported difference concerned attribution of the 9/11 attacks, despite official investigations establishing al-Qaeda’s responsibility, the report said. Among the surveyed groups, the data show that 62.24% of non-Muslim respondents identified al-Qaeda as responsible for 9/11, compared with 23.56% of Muslim American respondents.
About 18.51% of Muslim American respondents expressed belief that the US government or the CIA had carried out the attacks, the survey found. Furthermore, 27.40% of Muslim American respondents said Zionists or Israel had been responsible, it said.
Generational divides and political affiliations formed a major part of the study’s findings. Younger respondents displayed uncertainty, while partisan groups differed over whether major threats are primarily foreign or domestic.
Among adults under 30, al-Qaeda attribution dropped to 40%, with 28.57% of younger respondents saying they were completely “unsure” who was responsible, which “leaves them highly susceptible to digital manipulation,” the JCFA said.
Political cohorts split on threat perceptions, the report said, adding that the isolated non-Muslim sample was anchored heavily by Republicans, at 57.97%, who maintained a “traditional external defense posture identifying Iran and radical Islamists as the primary danger.” A plurality of Muslim Americans, at 26.20%, named the CIA or US government agencies as the “single greatest danger for a future mass-casualty event,” it said.
The study also evaluated public tolerance for radical critiques of American foreign policy by tracking reactions to online political commentator Hasan Piker’s statement that “America deserved 9/11.”
Regarding Piker’s remarks, the report uncovered a stark divide, noting that 47.11% of Muslim Americans actively disagreed or strongly disagreed with the statement, compared with 71.33% of non-Muslims, while a combined 28.13% of Muslim Americans either agreed or strongly agreed, and 24.76% remained neutral.
The findings showed that this tolerance has bled into mainstream political extremes, where non-Muslim Republicans exhibited a 55.07% rejection baseline compared with 43% for Democrats, while independent voters formed a “centrist bulwark” by logging the highest rate of active disagreement with the statement, at 64.80%.
These divisions extend to attitudes toward whether schools should be required to teach a standardized 9/11 curriculum. Views on historical education showed that a combined majority of 62% of surveyed non-Muslims, led by 77.53% of Republicans, 66% of Democrats, and 60.80% of Independents, supported a government-mandated 9/11 curriculum, compared with 44.71% of Muslim American respondents, with more than one-third of the latter selecting a neutral response.
In a statement to The Jerusalem Post, Mansdorf said: “The results are very clear on two points: First, there is a significant lack of knowledge among younger people about who carried out the 9/11 terrorist attacks; and second, Muslim Americans, to a much greater extent than the US population as a whole, do not accept that the attacks were carried out by the Islamist terrorists of al-Qaeda.”
“Clearly, there is a need for greater awareness and education about the events of 9/11,” he said. “While there is a strong focus every year on commemorating the victims of the attacks, far less attention is paid to the perpetrators and the motivations behind the attacks.”

Why Hasan Piker has become a target for US Democrats
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-27
12:54:19 UTC
21:54:19 KST

Breadcrumb
Why Hasan Piker has become a target for US Democrats
If you follow US politics at all, you probably would have noticed the raging debate about the role of controversial Twitch streamer Hasan Piker in endorsing several candidates from the left of the Democratic Party. For most people over 35, your first questions will be: what is a Twitch streamer? Why is this man getting so much attention?
Twitch is a website where users livestream themselves. Before the Covid-19 pandemic, it was largely confined to niche gaming enthusiasts, but with billions of people stuck indoors, Twitch suddenly got a huge new audience. Streamers expanded beyond gaming into music, movies, art, and other topics and the biggest personalities became celebrities in their own right. Increasingly, Twitch began to resemble an evolution of television rather than simply a platform for watching nerds play video games.
Another big development is that the US right, aka MAGA, picked up on this new platform where millions of people spend hours of their time every week, and organised to make it a venue for the dissemination of right-wing discourse.
With their massive funding and advertising advantages, Twitch streamers with a MAGA agenda like Adin Ross and FaZe Banks gained massive followings, even though the overwhelmingly young Twitch audience wasn't their most natural ally.
That contradiction is where Hasan Piker came in. His early streams mostly featured him playing video games while talking about current affairs from his idiosyncratic leftist, anti-imperialist perspective. Along with him just being very charismatic and funny, it resulted in him having 3.1 million subcribers, a far larger and more organic following than any of the MAGA streamers he was effectively an alternative to.
In more recent years, some of his streams have focused on discussing political issues with other personalities, and even interviewing ‘Yemeni Timothée Chalamet’ during the 2024 Red Sea blockade.
This year, Piker’s young following has been large enough that he’s been able to mobilise support for outsider candidates in the Democratic Party. For instance, he’s widely considered to have played a crucial role in Zohran Mamdani’s NYC mayoral campaign.
Several other Democrats from the ‘democratic socialist’ wing of the parties have appeared on his stream in the last year, or have benefited from his fundraising efforts. The most prominent has been Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic nominee for the Michigan Senate election, who has even had Piker speak at his rallies.
But Piker’s most important intervention in that campaign was to publicise a clip of someone who sounds a lot like El-Sayed’s election opponent Jeremy Moss, saying that the “entire purpose” of his campaign was to ensure “continued United States support for Israel”, and that it’s not wrong for American Jews to “put Israel first” because the United States “is not our homeland.”
We’ve since had very bizarrely framed coverage. For example, in one piece published by the Washington Post, there is acknowledgement that experts have determined there’s no evidence the clip was edited by AI, spliced together or anything to indicate it’s not authentic; yet the conclusion is that AI content has “made it harder for voters to know what to believe.”
A couple of months ago I thought the liberal hysteria at the spectre of Hasan Piker had reached its peak when the UK banned him from entering the country due to the “risk [he] may pose to UK society.” But since then, the Democratic Party-aligned press in particular seems to have become somewhat obsessed with him.
It’s no exaggeration to say his name is being mentioned practically daily in mainstream coverage, as though he were a major player in US politics.
In the last few weeks, Piker has been condemned as “dangerous, malicious and antisemitic” by Hakeem Jeffries, the Democratic leader in Congress. Other Democratic Congress members have chimed in, with one saying Piker has a history of “hateful ideas and antisemitic remarks”, or claiming his rhetoric is “right out of the Nazi playbook”.
This all seems a bit much for a man who’s given lengthy speeches opposing antisemitism, or who recently squeamishly replied, “I’m a little too woke for this,” when Norman Finkelstein said on his stream that he “doesn’t talk to Israelis” after the Gaza genocide.
But of course, we have to directly address the issue here. Although his other leftist opinions may be controversial, the real sticking point against Hasan Piker is his principled and well-articulated opposition to the state of Israel. That’s the central thrust behind all of the attacks on him.
Underlying all of this is the severe anxiety that support for Israel in the United States is deteriorating across the board, but especially with Democratic voters, where it is now a ‘fringe position’. The number of Democratic voters who say they have a positive view of Israel is now 13%, which is lower than the percentage who support banning all abortions.
So how can the party leadership rationalise being so diehard in support of a position the vast majority of their members oppose? Right now, Hasan Piker has become their scapegoat. Similar to how a lot of Americans vastly exaggerate the amount of influence Vladimir Putin has in domestic US politics to avoid dealing with the uncomfortable fact that MAGA is homegrown, the Democratic establishment has convinced themselves that their members’ sharp turn against Israel is not because they’ve had to watch them commit a live-streamed genocide for almost three years; it’s because a witty Twitch streamer bamboozled them into it.
Daniel Lindley is a writer and trade union activist in the UK.

27 killed in back-to-back South Africa mass shootings (VIDEOS)
At least 27 people were killed and 26 wounded in two mass shootings in South Africa within hours of each other, prompting police manhunts.
The deadliest attack took place late Saturday at a bar in Wedela, southwest of Johannesburg, where eight gunmen reportedly armed with AK-47 rifles and pistols opened fire on patrons, killing 17 people and wounding 15.
According to the South African Police Service (SAPS), people were drinking inside and outside the bar when the attackers arrived at around 9:30 PM local time. They opened fire on those outside before entering the bar and continuing the rampage there. The suspects allegedly searched some patrons and took their cellphones before fleeing in two unidentified vehicles. Two other vehicles were set on fire.

Thirteen men and four women were pronounced dead at the scene, and the wounded were taken to hospitals. Footage posted online appears to show the moment the shooting began, with people abruptly falling silent mid-song, then screaming as gunshots ring out in the background.

Police have mobilized detectives and specialized units to hunt down the suspects. No arrests have been announced and the motive remains unknown.
Hours later, another mass shooting struck an entertainment venue in Lwandle, outside Cape Town, around 1,000 km (620 miles) away. Gunmen entered the establishment at around 2:00 AM Sunday and opened fire on patrons. Five people died at the scene and another five succumbed to their injuries in hospital, according to police. Eleven others were wounded; a search for the attackers has been launched.
The bloodshed comes amid South Africa’s longstanding struggle with rampant violent crime and gun-related killings. The country consistently has among the world’s highest homicide rates and has one of the highest in Africa. The massacres came just days after another mass shooting in KwaZulu-Natal province, near Durban, where gunmen stormed a house party and killed 11 people, including a pregnant woman.
Earlier this year, President Cyril Ramaphosa described organized crime as the “most immediate threat” to the country. In March, he authorized the deployment of more than 2,000 troops to support police in crime hotspots across five provinces heavily affected by gang violence and illegal mining: Eastern Cape, Free State, Gauteng, North West, and Western Cape.
Despite efforts to stem the violence, South Africa continues to record high levels of violent crime. The latest quarterly police statistics show 5,427 murders from April to June. While slightly down from 5,770 over the same period last year, the figure amounts to nearly 60 murders per day.
Ramaphosa condemned the shootings on Sunday, saying “it cannot go on like this,” as he vowed that the security forces will “pull out all stops” to tackle the violence. He said the authorities will use technology to help track the attackers, but stressed that broader action is needed to stop people from “just pick[ing] up guns and starting shooting people at random.”

Swiss voters reject tighter neutrality rules in referendum
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-27
12:45:42 UTC
21:45:42 KST

Swiss voters reject tighter neutrality rules in referendum
About 71 percent of voters oppose initiative to impose stricter limits on neutrality, projection suggests.
Swiss voters have overwhelmingly rejected a proposal to impose stricter constitutional limits on the country’s longstanding neutrality.
About 70 percent voted against the initiative in a referendum on Sunday, final results from the Federal Statistical Office showed.
Recommended Stories
list of 2 items
- list 1 of 2Iran shifts trade north to Caspian Sea as war impairs Strait of Hormuz
- list 2 of 2Switzerland’s neutrality vote is asking the wrong question
The result would preserve the government’s ability to impose sanctions and cooperate with NATO, the transatlantic military alliance whose members include most of Switzerland’s larger neighbours, rather than lock those choices into a narrower constitutional definition of neutrality.
The initiative sought to define Swiss neutrality as “perpetual and armed”.
It would have barred Switzerland from joining or cooperating with military and defence alliances unless the country was under attack or an attack was imminent while allowing sanctions against states at war only when approved by the United Nations Security Council.
Pro Switzerland, a group that campaigns for national sovereignty, organised the initiative, which was backed by the right-wing Swiss People’s Party (SVP), Switzerland’s largest party.
Supporters argued that joining European Union sanctions against Russia and expanding security cooperation with NATO had weakened the country’s traditional neutral role.
The SVP has accepted the defeat and said it currently had no plans for further action.
The Swiss government, parliament and nearly all major parties opposed the proposal, saying it would leave the country less able to respond to international crises.
The argument over neutrality sharpened after Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.
Switzerland largely adopted EU sanctions against Moscow, prompting criticism from Russia and from supporters of stricter neutrality, who said the Swiss government was taking sides.
Switzerland has been internationally recognised as neutral since 1815, and neutrality has formed part of its federal constitutional framework since 1848.
Current policy still allows the country to cooperate with other states on security and to join sanctions while remaining outside military alliances.
The vote, therefore, centred less on whether Switzerland should remain neutral than on how much freedom its government should retain in applying that principle as Europe’s security environment changes.

Lavrov unimpressed by German FM’s last-minute UNGA overture (VIDEOS)
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-27
12:44:34 UTC
21:44:34 KST

Lavrov unimpressed by German FM’s last-minute UNGA overture (VIDEOS)
German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul arrived at last-minute talks with Moscow with Berlin’s familiar anti-Russia script firmly in hand, Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov has said.
Wadephul requested the meeting on the sidelines of the 81st UN General Assembly at short notice, Lavrov said. Moscow squeezed him into the Russian diplomat’s packed Saturday schedule before his address.
Asked about the encounter, Lavrov said he invited Wadephul to explain what had prompted to him to ask for the meeting. It was the first direct bilateral meeting between the Russian and German foreign ministers since the escalation of the Ukraine conflict, in which Berlin firmly sided with Kiev.
“He took out his notes and read out a text that completely reproduced what Germany’s leaders publicly and officially say every day,” Lavrov said, saying he had expected something beyond Berlin’s familiar refrain that Russia is the aggressor. The underlying message, as Lavrov described it, was that Wadephul had “deigned” to engage Moscow and Russia should return the favor with concessions on Ukraine and guarantees for Black Sea shipping.
🇩🇪🇷🇺 Russian foreign minister mocks the German foreign minister:
Lavrov says Wadephul came and read from a note the standard talking points Germany has publicly declared for years. “I learned nothing new from this”
Funnily, Lavrov says Wadephul acted in an arrogant way: “Now I… https://t.co/H2cgyLoNuIpic.twitter.com/MmzoBa84ph
Wadephul, he said, also confronted him over an August drone incident in Leipzig that Berlin blamed on Russia without producing evidence.
Lavrov brushed off both complaints in his signature dry manner. He said Russia had not deliberately targeted commercial vessels, while pointing to documented Ukrainian attacks at sea, and mocked Berlin’s readiness to pin drone incidents on Moscow on a “highly likely” basis.
Lavrov ultimately portrayed the meeting as a missed opportunity for substantive diplomacy.
“I honestly told him that I had thought he had something interesting, something unusual... I got nothing new out of it,” Lavrov said. Instead, he quipped, Berlin “could have simply called.”
An unwelcome report
Russian Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova later pointed to another telling detail: some apparently unwelcome reading material waiting for Wadephul at the table.
Placed before the delegations was a report titled “Heirs of Goebbels: Falsification of the Events in Bucha and Bloody Staged Performances of the Kiev Regime.” It lays out Moscow’s case that the 2022 Bucha killings were staged by Kiev and its Western backers. Ukraine and Western governments blame Russian forces for the alleged massacre. Videos circulated online appeared to show Wadephul promptly covering the report with his notebook upon taking his seat and ignoring it.
“Wadephul bashfully covered the report with his notebook and pretended he hadn’t noticed anything,” Zakharova wrote on Telegram, referring to its comparison with Nazi propaganda chief Joseph Goebbels. “Everything is perfectly obvious to everyone – the truth hurts.”
Meanwhile, Wadephul emerged from the meeting sticking firmly to Berlin’s established script, saying Germany was ready for dialogue if Moscow “is ready to give up its war against Ukraine.” He added that Europeans were not keen to leave talking to Russia entirely to Washington.
That concern is hardly surprising. Germany is a driving force behind the so-called “coalition of the willing,” which pushes continued support for Kiev and gained prominence as European capitals found themselves increasingly on the sidelines of diplomacy amid direct Russia-US contacts last year. Its members have continued arming Kiev while calling for greater military preparedness against a potential Russian threat – an approach Moscow has repeatedly criticized as hardly conducive to ending the conflict. Lavrov drove the point home at the UNGA, again rejecting claims that Russia plans to attack NATO or EU states and accusing European governments of militarizing for confrontation with Moscow.
Lavrov’s UNGA marathon
Disappointing as Lavrov evidently found his encounter with Wadephul, the German minister was just one stop in his diplomatic marathon spanning the geopolitical spectrum.
Lavrov’s New York interlocutors ranged from US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres and IAEA chief Rafael Grossi to officials from Serbia, Senegal, India, Uganda, Singapore, Sudan, Kuwait, Uruguay, Morocco, Iraq and Yemen.
Zakharova contrasted the packed schedule with Moscow’s increasingly frosty relations with Western Europe.
“We held dozens of talks at the UN. Heads of government and ministers from countries that the West disdainfully calls the ‘wild jungle,’ supposedly because of their low level of democracy, came to Sergey Lavrov,” she said, referencing former EU foreign policy chief Josep Borrell’s controversial 2022 metaphor comparing Europe to a “beautiful garden” and much of the rest of the world to a “jungle.”
Many encounters proved considerably warmer than Wadephul’s – and offered opportunities for Lavrov’s trademark dry humor. Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein traded jokes with Lavrov about being in “good shape” and the Russian diplomat’s “beautiful eyes.”
Swiss Foreign Minister Ignazio Cassis prompted another quip while posing for a photo with Lavrov.
“I hope they don’t fire you for this photo,” Lavrov joked. “I hope so too,” Cassis replied with a smile.
The banter came against a more serious backdrop. Switzerland is due to vote on Sunday about enshrining neutrality in its constitution, while Moscow has accused Bern of abandoning its traditional neutrality by aligning with Western policy on Ukraine.
Still, the contrast was stark: while Wadephul brought what Lavrov derided as Berlin’s same tired script, the rest of his UNGA marathon painted a far warmer picture of Russia’s ever-widening diplomatic engagement.

Swiss voters reject initiative to preserve neutrality
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-27
12:42:28 UTC
21:42:28 KST

GENEVA, September 27. /TASS/. Swiss voters rejected an initiative in a referendum that would have enshrined the principle of perpetual and comprehensive neutrality in the Swiss Constitution, as well as lifted anti-Russian sanctions and prohibited Switzerland from joining NATO.
According to preliminary results published by the Federal Statistical Office, 68.6% of voters opposed the initiative, while 31.4% supported it. Voter turnout was 46.36%.
For the initiative to pass, a double majority was required, meaning support from a majority of voters and a majority of cantons. Since 13 out of 26 cantons, including three half-cantons, have already voted against the initiative, it is clear that it has failed. Final results are expected this evening.

Etna erupts again: chaos at Catania airport, risk of higher air fares
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-27
12:39:01 UTC
21:39:01 KST

Mount Etna has resumed volcanic activity. Flights to and from Catania are suspended until Sunday because of ash. Unions protest over disruption caused by diverted services to other Sicilian airports.
Catania-Fontanarossa airport has once again been brought to a standstill because of volcanic activity on Mount Etna, which has forced the authorities to halt flight operations. Sac, the company that manages the airport, has announced the closure of the relevant airspace because of the heavy emission of ash into the atmosphere and unfavourable wind conditions.
All arrivals and departures have officially been suspended until 23:59 on Sunday 27 September. Flights were initially halted until 12:00, before the stop was extended. In a bid to limit disruption, the company has urged passengers not to go to the terminal without first checking the status of their flight with their respective airlines.
On Saturday the shutdown had serious repercussions across the entire regional transport network. The suspension of flights has in fact triggered a domino effect at other Sicilian airports such as Comiso, Palermo and Trapani, which suddenly became congested with the many aircraft diverted there in emergency. The handling of this situation, which left thousands of travellers stranded and searching for alternative solutions, quickly turned a logistical breakdown into an economic and industrial-relations dispute.
Risk of speculative air fares and criticism from trade unions
The paralysis has provoked a strong reaction from associations, which denounce the risk of speculation on air fares at a moment of great vulnerability for citizens. Acli Terra has reported abnormal increases and prohibitive costs for flights to and from the island, highlighting extreme cases such as a Verona–Palermo route shooting up to around 1,180 euros. Emphasising that a natural emergency must not be allowed to turn into economic damage for families, the association has called on the authorities to monitor price rises, stressing that the ability to manage recurring events directly affects the credibility and reputation of the Sicilian system as a whole.
In the same vein, transport unions are pointing the finger at organisational shortcomings, describing the situation as "total chaos". Filt Cgil, Fit Cisl and Uiltrasporti Sicilia express dismay at the absence of any contingency plan for an Etna eruption, a phenomenon they now consider structural rather than unforeseeable. According to the unions, those paying the highest price are airline and ground staff, forced to face passengers' exasperation in conditions of extreme stress and without clear guidelines.
The unions are therefore once again urging the Region to sign a permanent protocol that would establish reliable operational flows and adequate protections, finally moving beyond the ineffective logic of constant emergency.

Saudi strike on Yemen's Taiz kills seven
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-27
12:36:48 UTC
21:36:48 KST

Breadcrumb
Saudi strike on Yemen's Taiz kills seven
A Saudi airstrike on Taiz in southwest Yemen killed seven people and wounded dozens more, Houthi media reported on Sunday.
The Iran-backed Houthis' Al-Masirah TV channel said the strike killed seven and wounded 40 in a central marketplace in Taiz, minutes after reporting that a Saudi fighter jet had targeted the area.
Following years of relative calm, Yemen's war reignited in July, against the backdrop of the widening Middle East war.
Fighting intensified in September as the Houthis launched a lightning offensive that saw them seize Yemen's entire Red Sea coast, including the Bab al-Mandab Strait, a vital shipping lane.
The Houthis have in parallel launched a blockade on Saudi energy exports, already choked off by Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz.
On Saturday, Saudi Arabia said it intercepted two Houthi drones that were heading in the direction of the capital Riyadh.
Schools in Riyadh announced on Sunday that they would be shifting to remote learning for a week, without giving a reason, according to messages emailed to parents and seen by AFP.
Taiz, a major city controlled by the internationally recognised government, has been thrust to the frontlines of fighting between the Houthis and government forces.
Yemen's war erupted in 2014, when the Houthis seized the capital Sanaa from the Saudi-backed government, before going on to take control of vast swathes of the country's north.
Despite Saudi backing, Yemen's government forces have been unable to repel the latest Houthi offensive.
Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree nonetheless reported on Saturday that Saudi air forces launched 27 strikes targeting Taiz, Marib, Saada, Amran, Ibb and Hajjah provinces.

Budanov Announces Major POW Exchange With Russia as Early as Next Week
Unknown

2026-09-27
12:35:45 UTC
21:35:45 KST

Ukraine and Russia are reportedly preparing another major prisoner of war (POW) exchange, according to the head of the Presidential Office, Kyrylo Budanov Sunday, Sept. 27.
The exchange could take place as early as next week, Budanov told Novyny.LIVE on the sidelines of the national “Golden Hands” award ceremony.
JOIN US ON TELEGRAM
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
“It should happen very quickly, in the near future. I think, within the next week,” Budanov said according to RBC-Ukraine, without providing any additional information regarding the possible date or scale of the exchange.
Moscow had not independently confirmed the planned swap at the time of the report.
A rare channel of dialogue
Prisoner exchanges have remained one of the few areas where Kyiv and Moscow continue to cooperate, even as broader peace efforts stall, according to Budanov on Aug. 29.
He also said that the war in Ukraine will most certainly continue through the winter, dismissing hopes of a near-term ceasefire and saying that Russia’s refusal to stop the war made any immediate freeze “unrealistic.”
Previous swaps
The last known return took place on Aug. 24, when Ukraine brought home 10 servicemen from captivity via Belarus, according to RBC-Ukraine.
The release was carried out as a special stage of an exchange agreed between the two sides.
All 10 had fought in the Donetsk sector and had previously been listed as missing, two of them since 2024 and eight since 2025.
Could Central and Eastern Europe Present Itself as One Economy?
Just two weeks earlier, on Aug. 10, Ukraine and Russia exchanged 103 prisoners each. On Ukraine’s side, the released POWs included troops from the Armed Forces (AFU), Border Guard Service, and National Guard who fought in Mariupol and across several other regions.
In April, Budanov announced a new exchange was being prepared shortly after Ukraine brought home 182 people in its 72nd prisoner swap.
That group included 175 military personnel and seven civilians, many of whom had been in captivity since 2022, among them defenders of Mariupol and the Chornobyl Nuclear Power Plant.
At the time, Budanov said a larger group could not be returned right away because of what he described as bureaucratic delays on the Russian side.
Foreign citizens dragged into Russia’s war
According to Ukraine’s “I Want to Live” project – which helps Russian soldiers surrender – one in 10 POWs held in Ukraine is a foreign citizen.
As of September, Russian POWs in Ukraine include citizens of 55 countries.
Nearly 29,000 foreign nationals have signed contracts with Russia’s armed forces since the beginning of the full-scale invasion in 2022, pointing to the growing international outreach of Russia’s military recruitment which deliberately targets economically vulnerable people from Third World countries.
Russia had also signed a defense pact with North Korea on June 19, 2024, with both countries officially recognizing North Korean troop deployments in April 2025.
Since then, North Korean troops have continued to be deployed or rotated through Russia. Ukrainian military intelligence estimates that around 25,000 North Korean troops have served in Russia so far.
On July 29, Zelensky warned that Russia is preparing to receive 30,000 additional North Korean troops and more ballistic missile launchers.
In August, Kyiv had warned of Pyongyang’s fresh troop deployments to Russia, numbering 8,500.

ADB approves 100-mln-USD loan for affordable Bangladesh housing finance
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-27
20:35:35 CST
21:35:35 KST

DHAKA, Sept. 27 (Xinhua) -- The Asian Development Bank (ADB) has approved a concessional loan of 100 million U.S. dollars for a project to expand access to affordable and resilient housing finance for low- and middle-income borrowers in Bangladesh, particularly women.
The project will address a significant shortage of safe and affordable housing and limited access to housing finance for households with informal incomes who are not typically served by conventional mortgage lenders, the Manila-based lender said in a statement on Sunday.
"Housing is a critical foundation for dignity, opportunity, and resilience," said ADB Country Director for Bangladesh Qingfeng Zhang.
"By helping low- and middle-income families, especially women, invest in safer and more resilient homes, this project will contribute to Bangladesh's broader goals of reducing poverty, strengthening social protection, enhancing human development, and fostering more inclusive and sustainable economic growth," he added.
By 2031, according to the ADB, the project is expected to have provided loans to at least 40,000 households, including at least 32,000 women and at least 24,000 borrowers residing in areas vulnerable to natural hazards.
It will promote financial and land literacy, as well as housing rights awareness, while enhancing housing security for women through strict documentation of borrowers' spousal residency arrangements, said the lender. ■

China to work with all countries to build a community with a shared future for humanity: VP
China
Unknown Publisher

Chinese Vice President Han Zheng delivers a speech at the general debate of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly at the UN headquarters in New York on Sept. 26, 2026. (Xinhua/Pang Xinglei)
UNITED NATIONS, Sept. 27 (Xinhua) -- China will join hands with all other countries to build a community with a shared future for humanity and make the world a better place for all, said Chinese Vice President Han Zheng on Saturday.
Han made the remarks when delivering a speech at the general debate of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly.
The world is witnessing intertwined changes and turbulence, protracted geopolitical conflicts, widening development gaps and a growing number of global challenges, he said.
Noting that Chinese President Xi Jinping put forward the Global Development Initiative at the 76th Session of the UN General Assembly, and has since then proposed the Global Security Initiative, the Global Civilization Initiative and the Global Governance Initiative, Han said these initiatives provide strategic guidance for the building of a community with a shared future for humanity.
He said that more and more countries want to join hands to shoulder the historic mission of addressing difficulties and challenges, and advancing the well-being of all humanity.
Han put forward four proposals:
First, safeguard the postwar international order and foster lasting peace based on common security. Turn into action the vision of common, comprehensive, cooperative, and sustainable security, and reject the Cold War mindset and bloc confrontation.
Settle differences and disputes through dialogue and consultation, and oppose unilateral military actions that violate the UN Charter and circumvent Security Council authorization.
Second, address the global development predicament and promote prosperity for all through openness and cooperation. Keep development at the center of the international agenda, and jointly forge a global development partnership based on unity and equality and that is balanced and inclusive.
Give priority to key areas including poverty reduction, food security and energy transition, step up resource input, and increase support for countries in the Global South. Take a people-centered approach, strive for the positive and for good, and make efforts to narrow the digital divide.
Firmly safeguard the multilateral trading system, build an open world economy, and see that economic globalization is inclusive and delivers benefits to all.
Third, advance exchanges and mutual learning among civilizations and rebuild unity and mutual trust through communication and dialogue. Use the UN platform to boost international people-to-people exchanges, promote mutual understanding and amity among all peoples and the common development of diverse civilizations.
Reject ideological prejudice, and respect the development paths and social systems decided on independently by the people of all countries. Deepen the sharing of governance practices and jointly explore ways to tackle challenges facing our times.
Fourth, stay committed to multilateralism and take steps to safeguard fairness and justice. China holds that all countries, big or small, are equal members of the international community, and that world affairs should be handled by all through consultation, and rule of law, fairness and justice in international affairs should be jointly upheld.
Countries should join forces and act together to safeguard the UN and make it stronger. China supports the UN in reforming and improving itself, and in effectively addressing global challenges including climate change and public health security.
Han pointed out that the People's Republic of China restored its lawful seat in the United Nations in 1971, which is of profound and far-reaching significance for both China and the world.
Over the past 55 years, China has been a stabilizing force in times of volatility, he said, noting that China is firmly committed to pursuing peaceful development, and has the best track record on peace and security among major countries.
A main engine driving common development, China has created two miracles at home, namely, fast economic growth and long-term social stability, and it has, over many years, contributed around 30 percent to global growth, Han said.
He said that China, a progressive force in an era of change, has always stood up for the legitimate rights and interests of developing countries, and worked toward a more just and equitable global governance system.
Han said that no matter how the international dynamics evolve, China remains unchanged in its pursuit of peace and development, in its dedication to safeguarding fairness and justice, and in its commitment to multilateralism.
During his stay in New York, Han had separate meetings with Bulgarian President Iliana Iotova, Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic, Cypriot President Nikos Christodoulides, Ghanaian President John Dramani Mahama, and Kiribati President Taneti Maamau.
The presidents spoke highly of the major ideas and initiatives proposed by Xi, expressed admiration for China's development achievements, and reaffirmed their governments' firm adherence to the one-China principle.
They also expressed willingness to further enhance strategic mutual trust with China, deepen practical cooperation, strengthen multilateral coordination, and make greater contributions to the well-being of the people and global sustainable development. ■

Feature: Ethiopia celebrates Meskel with calls for national harmony amid renewed conflict
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-27
20:35:24 CST
21:35:24 KST

by Xinhua writers Habtamu Worku, Liu Fangqiang
ADDIS ABABA, Sept. 27 (Xinhua) -- Tens of thousands of people gathered on Saturday in Addis Ababa, the capital of Ethiopia, to celebrate Meskel, a major religious festival, hoping for national harmony and peaceful coexistence amid mounting uncertainties and concerns about a possible relapse into conflict.
FESTIVAL CELEBRATION
In Ethiopia, Meskel is celebrated annually on Sept. 27, or on Sept. 28 during a leap year, commemorating the discovery of the True Cross on which Christ was crucified on Good Friday. The Meskel Festival was inscribed on the UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage List in 2013.
The eve of Meskel, Sept. 26, is traditionally marked by burning a large bonfire, locally called "Demera" in Amharic, at the church, village, and household levels. This is a central act of the celebration for the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church.
As night fell on Saturday, religious and government leaders set the Demera bonfire ablaze in Meskel Square, located in the heart of the capital. The event featured the burning of a huge bonfire and a procession of priests, deacons, and Sunday School students performing spiritual chants and songs.
According to church accounts, the bonfire and procession commemorate how Queen Eleni was directed to the True Cross through a dream, in which she was told to start a bonfire and follow the smoke to where the cross was buried.
The colorful and elaborate celebration at Meskel Square was attended by archbishops, senior government officials, and diplomats, as well as tens of thousands of adherents and tourists.
In their addresses, senior Ethiopian government officials and religious leaders highlighted the East African country's rich cultural and religious heritage, calling for the fostering of national harmony and peaceful coexistence.
Ethiopia's Minister of Culture and Sport Shewit Shanka said that beyond its religious significance, Meskel plays an important role in preserving Ethiopia's history, identity, cultural values, and national unity.
"Ethiopia has made notable development gains in various sectors through hard work and the collective will of its people," the minister said, calling on Ethiopians to build on these achievements.
In his message issued on Saturday, Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed stated that Meskel is a religious and cultural festival celebrated throughout Ethiopia. He called on Ethiopians to unite toward fostering "a great national strength."
"Meskel has a family and social color. Families come together, the neighborhood gathers, the city and its surroundings converge on one square," Abiy said.
In Ethiopia, Meskel and other holidays are traditionally celebrated with unique customs, including the preparation of special traditional foods and drinks, and the exchange of seasonal greetings during visits with family and friends. The blooming yellow "Adey Abeba" flower has become a ubiquitous symbol of the celebration across the country.
MOUNTING UNCERTAINTIES
Despite the festive mood, recent tensions in the northern part of Ethiopia have raised concerns among the public, as well as international and continental organizations, about a possible return to conflict.
The East African country witnessed a deadly two-year conflict between Ethiopian federal forces and Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF)-loyal troops from November 2020 to November 2022. The ensuing war left millions in urgent need of humanitarian assistance before the two parties signed the landmark Pretoria peace accord in South Africa to end hostilities.
The latest escalation comes amid heightened tensions in Ethiopia's northernmost Tigray region, following the recent announcement of a new alliance formed by seven Ethiopian opposition and armed groups, according to local media.
On Friday, the United Nations expressed concern over the continued deterioration of the security situation in northern Ethiopia and the expansion of fighting along multiple fronts.
"We are particularly troubled by reports of the use of drones, as well as incidents of harm to civilians," said Stephane Dujarric, spokesman for UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres.
The African Union has also called for "utmost restraint and immediate cessation of all actions that could further escalate tensions," while urging the immediate resumption of direct talks within the framework of the Pretoria Agreement.
Amid the escalating security situation, the Ethiopian National Defense Force stated on Thursday that 272 TPLF rebel fighters were killed following the group's failed offensive on Tuesday night.
The Ethiopian army said in a statement that the forces "strongly repelled" the attack in the northeastern part of the country, eventually neutralizing several militants and seizing various types of weapons and ammunition.
According to the statement, the rebel group attempted to infiltrate the North Wollo zone in the country's Amhara region by deploying its forces across several districts, but was forced to retreat due to "the heavy blow it received, losing its assets and manpower." ■
