Vijay government exempts Tamil Nadu Public (Law &amp; Order) department from RTI- what it means
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-27
07:49:54 UTC
16:49:54 KST

NEW DELHI: The Tamil Nadu government led by CM C Joseph Vijay has exempted the Public (Law and Order) Department from the ambit of the Right to Information (RTI) Act, classifying it as an Intelligence and Security Organisation under Section 24(4) of the law.A Gazette notification issued by the state government places the department under the exemption framework applicable to intelligence and security organisations. The move means information held by the department will generally be outside the scope of RTI requests, subject to the statutory exceptions under the Act.
What the exemption means
The Public (Law and Order) Department deals with matters concerning policing, public order and law-and-order administration and RTI Act is a law to provide for setting out the practical regime of right to information for citizens wherein they can secure access to information under the control of public authorities.This exemption could therefore affect RTI requests seeking information relating to communal incidents, political agitations, police actions and other law-and-order matters handled by the department.The statement reads, "Gazette notification dated September 21, 2026, issued by the Human Resources Management Department, the Governor, exercising powers under Section 24(4) of the Right to Information Act, 2005, has specified the Public (Law and Order) Department as an "Intelligence and Security Organization" established by the Tamil Nadu government, "for which the said Act shall not apply."
However, Section 24 of the RTI Act does not provide a blanket exemption. Even organisations covered by the provision are required to provide information relating to allegations of corruption and human-rights violations, subject to the procedure prescribed under the law.Tamil Nadu has previously used the provision to exclude organisations including the Tamil Nadu State Vigilance Commission and the Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption.

Amit Shah flags off India's first LNG train in Gujarat, launches Rs 1,542 crore railway projects
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-27
07:49:11 UTC
16:49:11 KST

File photo: Amit Shah launches rail projects worth over Rs 1,542 Cr, flag off India's first LNG-powered train in Gujarat
NEW DELHI: Union home and cooperation minister Amit Shah on Sunday flagged off India’s first LNG-powered train in Gujarat and launched a series of railway projects worth more than Rs 1,542 crore at Sabarmati.The LNG-based train uses a diesel-LNG dual-fuel system, with two 1,400 HP Driving Power Cars at the Sabarmati Integrated Coaching Depot converted to run on both fuels. LNG can replace nearly 40 per cent of diesel consumption under the system.The initiative is aimed at reducing diesel use and fuel costs while lowering emissions including carbon dioxide, nitrogen oxides and particulate matter.The train was among several railway projects launched by Shah in Sabarmati, with the package also focusing on railway safety, line capacity and freight operations.Shah also laid the foundation stone for the indigenous Kavach automatic train protection system across 404 km of railway network in the Ahmedabad division.The project, estimated to cost around Rs 411 crore, covers 157 km of the Ahmedabad-Palanpur section and 247 km of the Ahmedabad-Samakhiyali section. Kavach is designed to help prevent train collisions, protect against overspeeding and reduce risks linked to human error.
An automatic block signalling system has also been introduced across 122.57 km of railway sections between Sabarmati-Kalol-Bhandu Motidau and Sabarmati-Sanand-Jakhwada at a cost of around Rs 118.83 crore. The system is designed to maintain safe distances between trains and increase route capacity.Shah also inaugurated the WAG-12 locomotive maintenance shed at Sabarmati, built at an estimated cost of Rs 700 crore.The facility will provide maintenance for 300 high-horsepower WAG-12 electric locomotives, which have a capacity of around 12,000 HP and are designed to haul heavy and long freight trains.The Sabarmati-Sarkhej railway line doubling project, estimated at Rs 313.27 crore, will cover a 21-km stretch and is targeted for completion by March 2028.
The project covers stations including Sabarmati, Gandhigram, Vastrapur and Sarkhej and includes bridges and road underpasses.The doubling is expected to improve train movement and connectivity towards the Sarkhej-Dholera region while supporting industrial and commercial activity in the area.The projects launched in Gujarat are aimed at improving railway safety, increasing operational capacity and promoting alternative-fuel technology in rail transport.

Switzerland: Referendum to decide on stricter neutrality
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-27
07:49:00 UTC
16:49:00 KST

Switzerland: Voters reject stricter view of neutrality
September 27, 2026
Voters in Switzerland look set to reject a proposal for stricter neutrality in a referendum held on Sunday, according to projections by state broadcaster SRF.
According to SRF figures, 29% voted for tighter rules on neutrality while 71% voted against adopting stricter measures.
Although Swiss neutrality has been recognized since the end of the Napoleonic wars in 1815 and part of the country's constitution since 1848, exactly how the government implements it is not clearly specified.
The initiative was brought forward by the Pro Schweiz association, a right-wing organization with links to the right-wing populist Swiss People's Party. They argue that the Swiss government has moved too close to the European Union and NATO since Russia's war in Ukraine.
What the Pro Schweiz Association wanted to achieve
The group said its aims were for:
- Swiss neutrality to be applied "permanently and without exception"
- Switzerland to maintain an army capable of defense
- Switzerland not to get involved in conflicts between third parties
- Switzerland not to join a defense alliance unless attacked
- The UN to approve any sanctions before Switzerland joins them
Swiss sentiment on neutrality
According to a poll by the Swiss Broadcasting Corporation (SBC) earlier this month, the move toward a stricter interpretation of Swiss neutrality does not have the traction needed to pass a referendum. Some 63% of respondents said they intend to vote against the initiative, while 34% plan on backing it.
Nearly all major political parties rejected the initiative, with the exception of the hard-right Swiss People's Party (SVP).
"Our goal is to foster peace, diplomacy and dialogue," SVP vice president Celine Amaudruz said during a televised debate. "To achieve that, we must maintain credibility through perpetual armed neutrality."
Swiss foreign minister: Neutrality needs 'degree of flexibility'
Opponents of the initiative argued that in the modern world a country cannot hide behind neutrality and treat perpetrators and victims equally.
"Neutrality has always been applied with a degree of flexibility," Swiss Foreign Minister Ignazio Cassis insisted during a recent televised debate.
In-person voting will begin at 10:00 am (0800 GMT) and polling stations close at noon. The result should become clear around an hour later.
Another referendum on food security has also taken place with that initiative calling for the Swiss population to have access to enough high-quality and affordable food at all times.
According to SRF figures 28% of voters supported the initiative and 72% rejected it.
The food initiative seeks to have Switzerland produce significantly more of its own food.

Renewables gain larger share of Türkiye’s installed power capacity
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-27
07:49:00 UTC
16:49:00 KST

AA Photo
Renewable energy sources accounted for 79,902 megawatts of Türkiye’s total installed electricity capacity of 126,944 megawatts as of the end of August, representing 62.9 percent of total capacity, according to the Energy and Natural Resources Ministry.
The ministry said domestic energy sources accounted for 72.1 percent of total installed capacity during the same period.
Installed solar power capacity rose to 27,914 megawatts by the end of August, equivalent to 22 percent of total installed capacity. Wind power capacity reached 15,434 megawatts, accounting for 12.2 percent of total capacity.
Combined installed solar and wind power capacity increased to 43,348 megawatts, representing 34.2 percent of Türkiye’s total installed electricity capacity.
Energy and Natural Resources Minister Alparslan Bayraktar said in a post on his social media account that Türkiye continued to strengthen its energy infrastructure.
Türkiye’s installed electricity capacity reached 126,944 megawatts as of the end of August, Bayraktar said.
“While 62.9 percent of this capacity comes from renewable sources, we have reached a total installed capacity of 43,348 megawatts in solar and wind energy,” he said.
“The share of solar energy in our installed capacity has increased to 22 percent. We will continue to expand the share of our clean, domestic and renewable resources day by day,” Bayraktar said.
He added that Türkiye would accelerate renewable energy investments, particularly in solar and wind power, to strengthen energy supply security and advance steadily toward its 2053 net-zero emissions target.
“During COP31, we will strongly demonstrate Türkiye’s vision and concrete targets in this field. We will continue working for a fully energy-independent Türkiye,” Bayraktar said.
According to ministry data, the number of electricity generation facilities in the country, including unlicensed plants, rose to 43,844 as of the end of August 2026.
Of the existing facilities, 777 are hydroelectric plants, 69 are coal-fired plants, 418 are wind farms, 68 are geothermal plants, 353 are natural gas plants, 41,749 are solar power plants and 410 generate electricity from other sources.
Türkiye’s electricity consumption increased by 2.1 percent year-on-year to 360.9 terawatt-hours (TWh) in 2025, while electricity generation rose by 2.4 percent from the previous year to 362.9 TWh.
According to the results of the Türkiye National Energy Plan, electricity consumption is projected to reach 455.3 TWh in 2030 and 510.5 TWh in 2035.

16:45:44 KST

In Switzerland, Panter&Tourron are designing subtle, quiet objects that people can’t help but take notice of. It would be unfair to say that their work is ‘eye-catching,’ as that may conjure an image of something gaudy, gold, or strobing. But there is a certain attention their work whispers for – a kind of if-you-know-you-know type signaling. Chatting with the studio’s founders, designers Stefano Panterotto and Alexis Tourron, they recall the funny places they’ve seen their work pop up, from a Balenciaga candle on supermodel Bella Hadid’s coffee table to their lamps in a futuristic Apple TV show. Yet speaking to the two, dressed in the types of dark sweaters that are almost archetypal of the industrial design type, there’s a keen sense that they do not have the spotlight in mind when creating their work.
In conversation with designboom, Stefano Panterotto of Panter&Tourron recounts creating a few home objects for Balenciaga back in 2022 when Demna was creative director and Martina Tiefenthaler was the brand’s Chief Creative Officer. He looks back fondly on the process, recognizing how at the time, the Spanish fashion house derived its aesthetic by mixing ‘a lot of ironic and functional things, very far from the typical fashion aesthetic references,’ and how that reflected the values of Panter&Tourron.
‘We designed it in a bubble in our studio in the not-so-glamorous Lausanne (compared to Milan or Paris),’ he says, speaking to the contrast between where they work and the flashier European fashion capitals. So when the candles and the lunch sets they created started popping up on their social media feeds, it came as a happy, albeit unexpected, surprise. ‘We never thought that it would appeal to a whole world of influencers and fashion lovers,’ says Panterotto, still with a hint of shock. ‘It was very funny to see it out there.’
From the beginning, when the two met during their graduate studies at the Swiss art and design school École cantonale d’art de Lausanne (ECAL), they recognized that the country would come to shape their future design sensibilities. ‘I studied and worked in Italy, Alexis in France, both countries with strong design heritage,’ Panterotto points out before going on to emphasize how the Swiss approach to industrial design, in fields like watchmaking and performance, expanded their ideas of what the field could be.
After graduating from ECAL, the two decided to open their own studio. ‘At the very beginning, we worked in the world of luxury where there are high-profile clients or really wealthy buyers behind it.’ Panterotto explains, ‘but in a way, it’s also a very private world. It’s less ‘out there’ and Switzerland is also very privacy driven in term of wealth and who buys what.’
Signal, their ceramic table lamp, appeared in the Apple TV show, Silos | image courtesy of Raawii
The ‘new codes’ of luxury
‘We underestimated how much scarcity and material richness still defined luxury for people,’ Tourron says of the old ‘codes’ of luxury they discovered when they entered the field. They didn’t see themselves in this language of ‘traditional, polished materials like gold,’ that was standard of the high-end sector. ‘It pushed us to be even clearer about high-end manufacturing and performance in our own work.’
In their years of practice, the two have worked to reassess and redefine these ‘codes.’ Tourron goes on to elaborate that it comes from a movement ‘towards truth to material, performance, and quality, focusing on where and how things are made and produced.’
The studio has returned time and time again to Hermès window displays, their careers’ earmarked by the brightly colored storefronts. In comparing his previous work in tech, where the culture was really fail fast and fail often, Tourron brings up how, ‘in luxury, it is called ‘high-end’ because everything is really double-and triple-checked, like the quality of the craftsman you can collaborate with, the assembly details, the materials sourcing, etc.’
The two came to learn that, in this environment, storytelling was often just as important as the product itself. ‘You can create an excellent product, but to sell it for that price you need more than a perfect product; you have to have an amazing story too,’ reflects Tourron.
Part of that story is the vibe that their designs create. They touch on their installation Softscope, a massive purple, pyramidal sitting structure that was presented at Spazio Maiocchi during Milan Design Week 2023. ‘Because of COVID, it was the first design week after two years where people could gather again,’ remembers Panterotto. ‘The ideas were around how people would use it throughout the week: would people actually gather there, use it as meeting point, spend long time, short break?’ With both Softscope and Studio di pittura’s Diurno lounge space, another Milan Design Week installation the studio worked on, Tourron says ‘people really came and stayed for a long time in both cases. It was a very happy surprise for us.’
There’s a quality to their work that makes it deceptively simple. Their Hall floor lamp is a bisected tube. Softscope was foam seating. Their exhibitions have an ease to them that photograph beautifully in their bright colors, but have a simplicity that allows their seating, wall coverings, and light fixtures to easily be transposed into most domestic spaces. Reflecting on the studio’s practice, the classic quote from Don Norman’s The Design of Everyday Things comes to mind: ‘good designs fit our needs so well that the design is invisible.’ This sentiment, although profound, puts a dilemma in front of many designers practicing today, where being seen at a brand dinner or in a museum showcase feels imperative to making a place for oneself in the contemporary ‘scene,’ that takes place as much in digital images as it does in real life.
Yet in their pursuit of new codes, ones that focus on how things are made and how they are experienced in real life, Panter&Tourron create a compelling case for trusting the process.
This interview is part of designboom’s SPECTATOR AND SPECTACLE chapter, asking how wonder gets built, presented in partnership withSolidNature, and how it might return some mystery to a world that has measured most of it away. Discover more stories that turn onlookers into participants, alter perception and disrupt the everyday here.
the first stop of our new travelling series brought together designers, architects, collaborators, and friends for a week of conversations and hands-on activities.

China sends two giant pandas off to Atlanta zoo after Xi-Trump summit

Unknown Publisher

China sends two giant pandas off to Atlanta zoo
September 27, 2026
Two giant pandas departed China's southwestern city of Chengdu for new home in Atlanta as part of an agreement between Washington and Beijing.
Chinese President Xi Jinping announced that the pandas would be relocated to the capital of the US state of Georgia during his three-day summit with US President Donald Trump in Washington.
Xi said the panda loan program was an example of "friendship between the Chinese and Americans."
The loan was one of the few concrete things to come out of the summit. China has long used pandas as a key part of its global diplomatic outreach, turning such agreements into a well-tested tool of soft power. On the flip side, Beijing has also let agreements lapse and pulled pandas back from countries when tensions arise.
Meet the pandas
Ping Ping and Fu Shuang, two adult pandas, will be on loan to Zoo Atlanta for 10 years, as part of the agreement. Both pandas were born in 2020 and have lived at the Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding.
A farewell ceremony was held before their departure.
Ping Ping, who is male, Fu Shuang, female, departed from Chengdu Shuangliu International Airport on a chartered flight around 3:00 a.m. on Sunday (1900 GMT on Saturday).
The FedEx-operated Boeing 777 was equipped with steamed corn buns, bamboo shoots and carrots to keep the animals nourished during their journey, Chinese media reported. They are also being accompanied by experienced US zoo keepers who had traveled to China ahead of time.
In preparation of their arrival, Zoo Atlanta renovated its panda facilities and ensured a long and stable supply of locally grown bamboo. The zoo has decades of experience with pandas, hosting the animals between 1999 and 2024.

Vice President Cevdet Yılmaz has stated Türkiye’s financial markets remain much stronger despite recent turbulence affecting only a limited segment of the capital markets.
Speaking at an event in the province of Elazığ on Sept. 26, Yılmaz referred to troubles in the investment funds market and said authorities were taking the necessary administrative and judicial measures to address the issue.
“Our financial markets are in a much better place, but we are facing a problem that has emerged in a specific and limited area of our capital markets,” Yılmaz said.
He added that the necessary administrative and legal steps were being taken and would continue to be implemented to overcome the problem.
“This is a temporary problem that has emerged in a limited area. Once we overcome it, our capital markets will continue on their path even stronger than before,” Yılmaz said.
“We are not facing a structural problem. The structure of our capital markets is quite healthy. However, we have a temporary problem, and all relevant institutions are fulfilling their responsibilities in coordination regarding this issue,” he said.
As part of the ongoing investigation, the Istanbul Chief Public Prosecutor’s Office sent a formal request to the Central Securities Depository (MKK) to determine the flow of funds and investor transactions related to funds managed by seven investment companies.
Meanwhile, Justice Minister Akın Gürlek said on Sept. 26 asset freezes were imposed following an examination of fund-related money outflows between July 1 and Aug. 16.
“Money outflows from the funds between July 1 and Aug. 16 were examined, starting with the highest amounts, and the assets of 46 legal entities, 18 funds and 42 individuals have been frozen,” Gürlek said.
The Capital Markets Board (SPK) announced last week that 131 investment funds set for liquidation currently hold approximately 826 billion Turkish Liras across 455,758 investors.
Dozens of people, including executives of some investment management companies, have already been arrested in the investigation.

Israeli projects for disabled children place first, second in Helen Hamlyn Center Fixperts awards
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-27
07:44:08 UTC
16:44:08 KST

Two projects by Israeli students of the Holon Institute of Technology (HIT) won first and second place in the Helen Hamlyn Center for Design’s 2026 Fixperts Awards, which connect students to people with disabilities in order to foster the development of practical solutions to everyday problems.
The first-place winner, "Ziv's Bike," was developed by Shai Sheinfeld and Roy After for 5-year-old Ziv Cohen.
Cohen, who suffered a stroke at the age of four months, has hypertonia in his left arm and leg. The project was designed to allow Cohen to ride a bike independently, without adult assistance.
Sheinfeld and After provided an adjustable pedal on the bike to keep Cohen's foot secure, as well as a handlebar extension for better control.
Second was the "Breathing Training for Yarin" project, developed by Noga Tzur and Uri David for 11-year-old Yarin Mosseri.
Mosseri, who has cerebral palsy, developmental delay, and epilepsy, needed to practice controlled exhalation in order to learn how to speak.
Tzur and David's project included a device that supported Mosseri's posture while he practiced and a variety of mouthpiece attachments for different exercises.
Project leader praises Israeli victory amid academic boycott
"The Helen Hamlyn Center is one of the world leaders in the field of inclusive design, and this year two of our students’ projects won first and second place," Prof. Gad Charni from the Design Faculty at HIT, who is leading the projects, said.
"This is significant international recognition of the quality of the projects we have been carrying out for over a decade, and is especially notable in the current period, against the backdrop of the academic boycott of Israel. Academics who attended the ceremony noted the high level of the works and estimated that they could have stood the level of master’s degree final projects.”

Class of IDF drone that killed two soldiers has history of explosive failures - report
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-27
07:44:03 UTC
16:44:03 KST

The "Atalef" (bat) style suicide drone, which was involved in the recent accident that killed two IDF soldiers, has had repeated incidents of failure in the past, N12 reported on Saturday.
According to N12, drones of that type had failed to detonate on at least seven prior occasions, and in another three incidents in 2025 had exploded while being examined by IDF forces.
After several investigations into these incidents, the Yahalom Unit released a series of safety guidelines for the Atalef drones, including explicitly instructing soldiers not to approach or move fallen drones, and instead call in bomb disposal forces.
On Friday, two IDF soldiers were killed when a drone that they were operating landed and exploded within their military outpost in the northern Gaza Strip, the military said.
Zamir establishes team to investigate explosive drone accident
IDF Chief of Staff Lt.-Gen. Eyal Zamir ordered the establishment of an expert team to investigate the operational accident in which the two soldiers were killed.
The team, led by a ground forces brigadier-general, will examine the incident in order to ensure a similar one does not occur again.
In addition, following the accident, the IDF grounded all attack drones for 48 hours, after which it will conduct a renewed assessment.
The Atalef suicide drone involved in the incident has been in operational use by the IDF since the start of the war.

What to know about Lourdes, one of Catholicism’s most famous pilgrimage sites
The site near the Spanish border draws millions of pilgrims annually, including sick and disabled believers hoping for a cure from the famed spring water in the Lourdes grotto. Here is what to know about Lourdes, one of Catholicism’s most important pilgrimage sites.
Lourdes’ popularity is intrinsically linked to Bernadette Soubirous. A young girl who came from a modest background, she was uneducated, with no knowledge of religion, and suffered from asthma when she reported 18 visions of a lady dressed in white in the Grotto of Massabielle near Lourdes, between February and July 1858. The Catholic Church later accepted that the visions were of the Virgin Mary.
Bernadette’s visions, and the subsequent discovery of allegedly healing spring waters, led the church to build a sanctuary there.
🎥 Pope visit expected to boost Lourdes economy
The town of Lourdes in southern France is the second stop on Pope Leo XIV’s visit to the country, following his time in Paris. Around 150,000 people are expected to attend a mass led by the pontiff at the Sanctuary of Our Lady of Lourdes on Sunday.
Local businesses are hoping the influx of visitors will also boost the economy, as pilgrims spend money on souvenirs, food and other goods.

How is drone warfare changing rapidly? An IDF interceptor explains what's next
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-27
07:43:53 UTC
16:43:53 KST

In the latest episode of the Jerusalem Post's Defense & Tech podcast, host Anna Ahronheim sits down with Michael Cukierman, who heads the defense division at Cukierman & Co and carries a rare double résumé: a former IDF commander specializing in drone interception, and an investment banker who now shepherds Israeli defense companies into international M&A deals.
That combination, battlefield to boardroom, is what makes the conversation so compelling. Cukierman traces how the drone threat mutated in real time over the course of the war: from commercial quadcopters Hamas bought off eBay and Amazon, to Hezbollah's 3D-printed DIY drones in the north, to today's fiber-optic drones that render jammers and cyber defenses useless and have triggered what he calls a billion-dollar race for a kinetic solution.
With Russia logging over 100,000 drone strikes in a single year and the IDF going from one drone per unit to one or two per squad, he makes the case that this is the defining weapons story of our era.
From the battlefield to the boardroom
The battlefield segment is full of details that reward watching rather than reading a summary. Cukierman walks through the four-layer interception "kill chain": detection, identification, decision, and interception, and reveals how brutally little time defenders actually have: as little as 15 seconds from spotting a drone to stopping it. He's candid about the failures too, admitting that early in the war a "messy sky" of uncoordinated drones led to friendly-fire interceptions of Israel's own aircraft.
He explains why the lab lies to investors: a laser that melts drones on a test range can be defeated by fog, weather, or even the vibration of a passing tank, and gives a clear-eyed verdict on Rafael's Iron Beam: devastating against predictable targets, far less so against small, maneuvering drones. His most contrarian point may be the one component he says nearly every company underestimates: the command-and-control layer that could tie rival systems into a single network.
Then the conversation pivots to the money, and it gets just as sharp. Cukierman recounts an eight-month tender with German defense giant Rheinmetall in which his Israeli client reached the final two, only to lose to a Ukrainian competitor on valuation, a window into why European buyers keep looking at Kyiv instead of Tel Aviv.
He argues Israel has a knowledge problem, not a technology problem, and shares how a single meeting turned a skeptical German strategic player into a new partner. There's the surprising economics of dual-use tech (drone-detection acoustic sensors that became hearing devices; laser interceptors that pivoted to welding), the "do or die" logic that keeps buyers coming even when governments say they won't, and a genuinely provocative forecast for 2030: an automated frontline of drones and autonomous systems, with human operators pulled back to the rear, a battlefield that, in his words, may be safer for soldiers even as it grows deadlier. It's a rare, unvarnished look at how tomorrow's wars will be fought and funded, and it's well worth the watch.

Taiwan takes Asian Games baseball bronze after beating China 5-1

2026-09-27
07:37:45 UTC
16:37:45 KST

TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — Taiwan defeated China 5-1 on Sunday to win the bronze medal in the men’s baseball tournament at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games.
Left-handed pitcher Lin Yu-min (林昱珉), who plays in the Arizona Diamondbacks’ Triple-A system, delivered a dominant performance, throwing eight scoreless innings while allowing just one hit and striking out 10. He retired the first 13 batters he faced, per UDN.
With a 90-pitch limit set by his club, Lin exited after throwing 81 pitches. Wang Cheng-hao (王政浩) took over in the ninth, surrendering one run before closing out the victory.
Lin’s performance was backed by 13 hits, with Chen Min-sih (陳敏賜) and Yang Po-hsiang (陽柏翔) each collecting two hits and two RBIs.
Taiwan took the lead in the second inning. After a single and a hit batter put two runners on base with two outs, ninth-place hitter Yang lined a two-run triple to give Taiwan a 2-0 advantage.
Taiwan maintained its lead through the middle innings before breaking the game open in the seventh. With one out, pinch hitter Yang Chen-yu (楊振裕) and Huang Wei-sheng (黃韋盛) hit consecutive singles. Chen then hit a two-run double with two outs, followed by an RBI double from Kao Yu-wei (高育瑋), putting Taiwan ahead 5-0, per UDN.
The victory came two days after Taiwan defeated China 9-1 in the Super Round. Taiwan missed the gold-medal game after losing 7-3 to host Japan in another Super Round matchup Saturday. Taiwan finished the round with a 1-2 record, setting up Sunday’s bronze-medal rematch with China.
Baseball became an official medal sport at the Asian Games in 1994. Taiwan’s medal haul now comprises one gold, four silver, and four bronze medals.

Multiple explosives arrests near RAF base, town evacuated
United Kingdom
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-27
08:36:49 BST
16:36:49 KST

A major incident has been declared near RAF Fairford after several men were arrested on suspicion of offences under the Explosives Act, with residents evacuated and an Army explosive ordnance disposal team examining a number of vehicles.
Gloucestershire Constabulary said a number of properties in the Whelford area were being evacuated following the declaration of the major incident.
“A number of properties are currently being evacuated in the Whelford area following the declaration of a major incident.
“It follows the arrest of several men on suspicion of offences under the Explosives Act.
“The Army’s specialist explosive ordnance disposal team are currently examining a number of vehicles.
“The local residents are being evacuated to a nearby leisure centre.
“A cordon is currently in place but we’d like to reassure people that we believe this incident is contained.
“We are working closely with our partners and are enacting the well-rehearsed plans we have in place.”
Images and local reporting from the area showed officers carrying out door-to-door evacuations around Horcott Road and nearby streets close to RAF Fairford.
RAF Fairford is a US Air Force-operated base in Gloucestershire used by the 501st Combat Support Wing and frequently supports deployments of American military aircraft to the UK. The incident comes against a background of heightened public interest in security at the base, although there is currently no official statement linking the arrests to RAF Fairford itself.
Separate social media reports published before the police announcement claimed force protection measures at Fairford had been increased, including claims that the base had moved to Force Protection Condition Delta.
A US Air Force spokesperson, responding to reporting about security at Fairford, said: “We are aware of the current reporting. For operational security reasons we will not discuss specific force protection measures.”
Force Protection Conditions are used by the US military to set security measures according to the assessed threat. Delta is the highest level and is normally associated with a terrorist attack having occurred or intelligence indicating an imminent threat at a specific location, but the US Air Force has not confirmed that Fairford is operating at that level.

Air quality worsened in the Kyiv region after the shelling — in which cities it is better not to open windows
Kyiv • UNN

As a result of enemy shelling, air quality has deteriorated in several cities in the Kyiv region; residents of Obukhiv and Brovary are advised not to open their windows until the situation improves, UNN reports, citing the Kyiv Regional Military Administration.
A temporary deterioration in atmospheric air quality was recorded in the cities of Obukhiv and Brovary as a result of enemy shelling. According to monitoring stations, the main pollutant at present is fine particulate matter
The Regional Military Administration added that prolonged exposure to it may cause breathing discomfort in older people, especially those with cardiovascular diseases, people sensitive to irritation, and children.

The level of gamma radiation in the Kyiv region is consistent with the natural background level.

China and US agree to continue key trade talks
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-27
07:29:20 UTC
16:29:20 KST

President Trump and China’s President Xi watch a flyover during a military review at the White House. AP Photo
China and the United States agreed to establish a channel for handling AI-related incidents and accelerate work on military crisis communications following a three-day summit between President Xi Jinping and President Donald Trump in Washington, the two governments said on Sept. 26.
They also agreed to continue cooperating through a Board of Trade focused on selected bilateral issues. The White House said the board began operating this week.
The summit produced no major breakthroughs, but analysts said the steps toward greater cooperation were important because they established working groups that could help prevent disputes from escalating.
During the visit, Trump displayed unusual warmth toward Xi, despite having escalated a trade war with China the previous year that had global repercussions.
The statement from China said both sides will continue to work together on the pledge to reduce reciprocal tariffs on roughly $30 billion worth of goods. During the summit, the two leaders agreed to extend a trade truce by two months. The White House statement said China agreed to import at least 10 million metric tons of coal from the U.S. in 2027 and 2028.
Most of the reduction in tariffs is aimed at non-sensitive goods, such as agricultural products or holiday decorations.
The statement from the White House said the two sides continued to work on American concerns about rare earths supply, “with the goal of ensuring shipment levels return to appropriate levels.” China put export controls on rare earths last year in response to the U.S. tariffs, cutting the supply sent to the U.S. and other countries.

Estonia’s Chamber of Commerce and Industry, major energy companies and government representatives have launched a study of the country’s future electricity needs, ERR reports.
The study will compare combinations of power generation, storage and cross-border connections at different levels of demand.
It aims to identify the investment needed for the most cost-effective mix and is due for completion by the end of February 2027.
An advisory council that includes participating companies and grid operator Elering will provide feedback, while a separate steering committee will approve the model’s assumptions and methodology.
The chamber says all technologies will be assessed on the same basis, with the findings made public when the study is complete.

Two mass shootings in South Africa leave at least 27 dead

Seventeen people were killed in a shooting at a bar to the west of Johannesburg, while 10 people were fatally shot in an attack outside of Cape Town, police said.
Two mass shootings in South Africa have left at least 27 people dead, police said on Sunday.
The SA Police Service reported that 17 people were fatally shot in an attack at a bar to the west of Johannesburg on Saturday night.
"It is alleged that patrons were drinking inside and outside the tavern when the suspects arrived and opened fire on those outside," the force said in a statement.
"The suspects then entered the tavern and continued shooting at patrons inside. The suspects were reportedly armed with AK-47 rifles and pistols. They allegedly searched some patrons and took their cellphones before fleeing the scene in two unidentified motor vehicles," the statement continued. "Two vehicles were also set alight during the incident".
It added that 13 men and four women were killed in the shooting, which took place at around 9:30 pm.
Local police have launched an investigation into the incident, with detectives and specialised units deployed to track the suspects. No arrests have so far been made.
In a separate incident, 10 people were killed and 11 were injured in a shooting in Lwandle, just outside Cape Town, in the early hours of Sunday morning, according to the SA Police Service.
"Official police reports indicate that gunmen entered an entertainment place that also sells braaied meat (shisanyama) at approximately 01:46 and shot at patrons," the service said.
"As a consequence, five individuals died on the scene while five others succumbed to injuries sustained after being transported to medical facilities. Eleven others are receiving medical treatment for injuries sustained," its statement continued.
Local police have opened investigations into murder and attempted murder. The identities of the victims are to be released after their next of kin are informed.

EIS to spend millions promoting Estonia and its e‑residency program worldwide
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-27
07:25:00 UTC
16:25:00 KST

EIS to spend millions promoting Estonia and its e‑residency program worldwide
The Estonian Business and Innovation Agency (EIS) is running several major procurements to market Estonia abroad, including up to €1 million for promoting the e‑residency program and up to €3 million for tourism business marketing.
EIS is seeking a partner who would handle sales promotion and business marketing of Estonia as a travel destination to wholesalers, tour operators, travel agents, and other companies, and who would also provide communication services. For this, EIS has allocated €3 million, to which VAT will be added, and the framework agreement will be concluded for up to two years.
The foundation measures the effectiveness of tourism marketing, among other things, by the contacts created, the number of visitors to Estonia, and the money they spend here. With the services procured, the awareness of Estonia as a destination should increase and demand for Estonian tourism should grow.
In addition, EIS launched this week a procurement with a volume of €1 million to find an implementer for communication of the e‑residency program. According to the procurement conditions, the partner's task will be to convey to foreign markets the message that Estonia is the fastest and most efficient way in the world to create and manage a European Union company regardless of location, and to position Estonia as a leader in the global business environment and digital entrepreneurship.
In September, EIS completed a procurement with a volume of €300,000 to find a provider of business marketing services on the Japanese and U.S. markets within the Beyond Nordics cooperation project. This is a project in which Estonia, Latvia, and two Finnish cities are introduced as a joint tourism destination to the U.S. and Japanese markets. The evaluation of bids is currently underway.
Visitors are projected to spend more during trips to Estonia
EIS's head of foreign tourism markets, Agnia Nast, said that the economic benefit to Estonia is assessed at several levels, and the broadest indicator is how much foreign visitors spend in Estonia.
"In 2025, this sum was €1.65 billion, which is 10 percent more than the year before. Together with the export revenue of Estonian passenger transport companies, tourism services export reached €2.21 billion," Nast said.
She added that these sums cannot be taken as the direct result of one campaign or procurement, because whether a person travels to Estonia is influenced simultaneously by many circumstances: flight and ferry connections, prices, the general economic situation, destination awareness, and the sales work of tourism companies themselves.
"Therefore, in addition to general tourism revenue, we also monitor results closer to our activities: what contacts we can create for Estonian companies, whether trips to Estonia reach the offerings of foreign tour operators, and whether new travel products, contracts, and sales emerge from cooperation. The impact on visitor numbers and spending may manifest only over a longer period," Nast said.
The funding source for the procurement is European structural funds. According to Nast, the four‑year agreement covers 15 markets from which there is the greatest potential to bring visitors to Estonia and increase tourism revenue. She emphasized that concluding a framework agreement means an opportunity and readiness, not an obligation to order.
"We decide specific activities and their volume according to how the market is doing, what connections exist with Estonia, where there is a lack of information about Estonia, and what contacts our companies need. Thus the procurement gives us the opportunity to act where and when it is most beneficial," Nast said.
10,000 new e‑residency applicants expected
According to EIS e‑residency program deputy head Katriin Alasoo, the reason for their communication procurement is that the state has set ownership expectations for the program, and the supervisory board confirms specific goals for the program each year.
"As a result of the procurement, we expect a strong partner on the UK market who would help us reach the target group effectively through media relations and events. The goal is to support the achievement of the program's strategic objectives and increase the number of new e‑residents," Alasoo said.
For next year, the e‑residency program has been given the goal of bringing 10,000 applications from various target markets, including the United Kingdom, and tax revenue of €102 million to the Estonian state.
Alasoo pointed out that currently there are more than 5,600 e‑residents from the United Kingdom, and with the help of international partners EIS wishes to grow this number steadily.
"1,576 companies have been created, and according to Statistics Estonia, last year companies of UK‑origin e‑residents generated an estimated €4 million in tax revenue," she said. "The United Kingdom is one of the three most important European target markets from which entrepreneurs create and manage companies registered in Estonia, thereby contributing to Estonia's economy and tax revenue growth."
She highlighted that this year, with the support of the UK PR partner, coverage has been achieved in several influential publications, such as Think Digital Partners, TechRound, Business Quarter, Startups Magazine, UK Tech News, and Euronews.
According to EIS, e‑residency is one of the highest‑yield programs for the Estonian state, and as of the end of August this year, the direct revenue created by e‑residency has exceeded €465 million.
"In 2025, every euro invested in the functioning of the program returned more than €12 to the state. In addition to tax and state fee revenue, e‑residency has brought Estonia significant international media attention, with an estimated value reaching hundreds of millions of euros," Alasoo said.
Bringing Japanese and U.S. tourists to Estonia important
The procurement for the U.S. and Japanese markets that ended in September is, according to Alasoo, connected to the Beyond Nordics program, which is carried out together with Finnish and Latvian partners. Together with partners, its budget is €2.8 million. 80 percent of the budget comes from the European Union's Interreg program.
"Estonia was invited into the project at Finland's initiative as a national tourism marketing agency in the region with notable experience on the U.S. and Japanese markets," Alasoo added.
According to her, U.S. and Japanese visitors are valuable for Estonia because their trips involve significant spending. At the same time, they have a long journey to Estonia, and here one must offer sufficiently strong and high‑quality experiences and good reasons to stay longer than one stop.
"Through Beyond Nordics we develop, together with entrepreneurs, travel products that connect several destinations and help bring them into the offerings of U.S. and Japanese tour operators. The goal of the project is to create new sales opportunities for our tourism companies, from which in the longer term more visits and tourism revenue would come to Estonia," Alasoo said.

Northern Ireland live: Orange Order march in Catholic part of Portadown after near 30-year ban

Gavin Robinson, leader of the Democrat Unionist Party, the biggest pro-U.K. party in Northern Ireland, has been holding a press conference.
He insists the Orange Order who had gathered at Drumcree Church at 8am for the controversial parade can wait hours, days, and months to march down Garvaghy Road.
“If it takes another 28 hours, if it takes another 28 days they will show the same steadfast determination and patience and a willingness to uphold the law that’s been there for the last 28 years,” Robinson told reporters in Belfast.
He also again criticised First Minister Michelle O’Neill, saying she was giving a “two finger salute” to the law.
“The people at home know how difficult this is. They have someone who calls herself the First Minister for all breaking the law, prepared to give a two finger salute to the rule of law and order in this country.”
In response to a ruling by Northern Ireland’s high court early on Sunday, that a Protestant parade may proceed through a Catholic area, hundreds of protestors and residents of Portadown blocked the controversial Orange Order march.
The DUP’s leaders attacked Sinn Féin politicians – First Minister Michelle O’Neill, and Sinn Féin president Mary Lou McDonald - for joining the protesters in Portadown blocking the route of the Orangemen march.
Michelle O’Neill described the court ruling as “disgraceful”, claimed an Orange procession was being ‘forced’ through the area and declared: “There is no going back. Not tomorrow. Not ever.” Those words were followed by organised obstruction of the road, with people instructed to sit down, link arms and return if removed by police.
Democratic Unionist lawmaker Jonathan Buckley described the blockade of protesters as being “led by mob rule”, and condemned the Republican politicians encouraging the demonstration. “There has been an attempt on Garvaghy Road today, by those who are led by mob rule, to try to upend what was a lawful decision by the courts.”
Gavin Robinson, leader of the Democrat Unionist Party, the biggest pro-UK party in Northern Ireland, held a press conference in which he insisted the Orange Order who had gathered at Drumcree Church at 8am for the controversial parade can wait hours, days, and months to march down Garvaghy Road.
Northern Ireland Secretary Sir Chris Bryant left the Labour Party conference in Liverpool and headed to Belfast amid the tensions. Bryant issued a caution when asked about O’Neill and McDonald, stating “I don’t think any elected politician should be supporting an unlawful protest.”
Bryant added that maintaining the resilience of the political system in Northern Ireland is of key importance and no one wants to “dismantle” the Good Friday Agreement.
PSNI chief constable Jon Boutcher has said he, and political leaders, are “trying to find a space” that can “resolve” the current standoff over the controversial decision over the Drumcree parade.
The Chief Constable of the Police Service of Northern Ireland has said: “I am hoping we will bring all of today’s events to a sensible and peaceful conclusion.”
On what a successful conclusion may look like, Jon Boutcher told reporters in Belfast: “There has got to be a longer-term conversation which involves politicians and the people involved in what we have seen in the last 24 hours, trying to find a space that they can resolve these issues.”
There had been many “sensible voices” calling for calm which he thought had been “listened to by all parties”.
The SDLP MP Colum Eastwood has called on Northern Ireland secretary Chris Bryant to “step in” and end the crisis over the Garvaghy Road parade crisis.
Bryant has said on multiple occasions today that he does not have the power to call off the parade without a request from the PSNI chief constable, Jon Boutcher.
Eastwood claimed there could be a route for Bryant to intervene decisively with the “risk of disorder” which is now present “in every town” in Northern Ireland providing him with a potential legal underpinning for the secretary of state.
Bryant cut his participation in the Labour conference in Liverpool short today to got to Belfast, immediately calling for “compromise”.
Eastwood said: “I have personally, forcefully, said to Chris Bryant today ... and last night, and most days this week, that he has to step in. This decision [by the Parades Commission] is wrong and he has a responsibility to take the heat out of this and just say we’re going to deal with this properly.”
He said Bryant had a “tough job” but it was the one in “front of him”.
An SDLP member of Northern Ireland’s assembly has said she is concerned that the Stormont executive will collapse amid escalation of tensions over the Drumcree parade.
“I don’t know if it will last until the end of the week,” she told a panel at the Labour party conference.
The MLA, from Derry, said the parade crisis had already raised the temperature across Northern Ireland with helicopters out in her city for the first time in a “long, long time”.
She described the ruling to allow the march as “senseless” and “abhorrent” and said it was “irresponsible” of unionism not to have walked the orange order away from the parade.
She questioned whether their “game plan” was to bring down the executive.
“At the minute, this instability and insecurity is in real danger of bringing down those institutions, and the people at least can afford that are the people that are living in poverty in our communities, and delivering living without proper public services,” she said.
The Northern Ireland Secretary declined to say whether First Minister Michelle O’Neill had broken the law by participating in a protest.
Sir Chris Bryant was asked about DUP leader Gavin Robinson’s earlier claim that O’Neill had broken the law by Sky News.
Bryant said: “I just want to make sure we have fully functioning, as normal as possible, executive and assembly, functioning, working trying to deliver public services for the people of Northern Ireland.
“It’s not my job to decide whether somebody has or hasn’t broken the law, that’s a matter for others. All I would say is that everybody should be co-operating with the police at the moment. That is everybody.”
He added those in public office had a “particular onus upon us to try and calm and bring temperate language to everything”.
No one wants to "dismantle" Good Friday Agreement, NI Secretary says
Maintaining the resilience of the political system in Northern Ireland is of key importance and no one wants to” dismantle” the Good Friday Agreement, according to Sir Chris Bryant.
The Northern Ireland Secretary told reporters in Belfast: “Nobody wants to go back to 28 years.
“I don’t think there is a single person involved in politics in Northern Ireland that really wants to go back 28, 30 years and relitigate everything and dismantle the Good Friday Agreement.
“I’m very determined that we will do everything to maintain that but we need to make sure that we have resilience in the political system here.”
He added: “I think it’s all the more important that we have a Parades Commission that is fully functioning. Of course, these issues were litigated in court at length yesterday afternoon and through into the night.”
Religious leaders from the Catholic Church and the Church of Ireland have issued a joint statement calling “for the urgent creation of a constructive, inclusive and reconciling initiative” to find a way through the current crisis.
Archbishop Eamon Martin, Catholic Archbishop of Armagh, and Archbishop John McDowell, Church of Ireland Archbishop of Armagh, said: “We share the conviction that the greatest commandment, and the greatest witness anyone can give to the Gospel in our world today, is in love of God and love of neighbour.
“As our community faces the crisis in Drumcree today, in which so many sincere views, painful histories and important issues are at stake, we cannot think of any time in the last thirty years when this simple message needs to be more urgently heard.
“As Church leaders, we are profoundly aware of our own failings and inadequacies. Imperfect as we may be, we feel deeply the concerns of the people of Drumcree and the wider community that we serve.
“We are willing to do all that we are asked to guide the feet of all, in the name, and after the example of Jesus, on the way of peace, and the building up of a better future for all. We call for the urgent creation of a constructive, inclusive and reconciling initiative to patiently find a way through this current crisis. Too much is at stake.”
PSNI chief constable Jon Boutcher has said he, and political leaders, are “trying to find a space” that can “resolve” the current standoff over the controversial decision over the Drumcree parade.
“That is what we need to do. I need to underscore the amount of sensible voices that have been calling for calm, which I think have been listened to by all parties,” he told reporters at an impromptu press conference in Belfast.
He said the last 24 hours had been “very challenging” and his priority was to keep everyone safe.
He said policing success would be to avert violence and ensure that “not one hair on one head gets harmed”.
“It is an ongoing police operation. I can promise you, it will only ever be proportionate,” he said.
Although he said he would not be “getting into it”, his officers had been “evidence gathering” ... “from the very start”.
“So whatever’s been happening by whatever party we’ve been gathering the evidence of what they’ve been doing. So we’ll deal with that at the right time.”
NI Secretary calls for everyone to “double down on compromise”
Northern Ireland Secretary Sir Chris Bryant has said everyone needs to “double down on compromise”.
Speaking to reporters in Belfast, Bryant said: “The whole idea of us coming here is to be able to try and be able to talk specifically face to face to some of the political leaders and some of the community leaders to see if we can get to a settled position.
“The truth is everybody has to double down on compromise – that’s what life’s all about – double down on compromise.”
Bryant, who travelled from the Labour Party conference in Liverpool to Belfast to address the tensions, said he has spoken to Prime Minister Andy Burnham.
The Northern Ireland Secretary Sir Chris Bryant has appealed for calm.
Speaking to reporters in Belfast, he said: “It is absolutely important that everybody cooperates with the police, that everybody takes a moment to maintain a degree of calm, to respect people who have a different opinion from yourselves and to be able to try and achieve some kind of resolution of what is obviously a very difficult situation today.”
Bryant said he had come from the Labour Party conference in Liverpool “specifically” to have meetings with other political and community leaders “if necessary”.
He said: “If there is a way of finding a way through this, we want to be able to put ourselves at the service of others to be able to achieve that.”
NI Secretary says elected politicians should not have joined protest
The DUP’s leaders have been attacking Sinn Féin politicians for joining the protesters in Portadown blocking the route of the Orangemen march.
Now Chris Bryant, the UK government’s secretary for Northern Island, has also issued a caution when asked about First Minister Michelle O’Neill, and Sinn Féin president Mary Lou McDonald being present.
“I don’t think any elected politician should be supporting an unlawful protest,” he told Sky News.

A major prisoner exchange could take place as early as next week: what the OP says
Kyiv • UNN
Kyrylo Budanov said that a new prisoner exchange could take place next week. The date and number of people were not specified.
Head of the Office of the President of Ukraine Kyrylo Budanov expressed hope that a new prisoner exchange could take place as early as next week. UNN reports this, citing Novyny.LIVE.
He did not name a specific date or the number of people planned to be returned.
Details
Answering a question about the prisoner exchange, the head of the Office of the President noted that news could emerge in the near future.
"It should happen very quickly, in the nearest future. I think, within a week," Budanov said.
When the journalist clarified whether he meant specifically next week, he replied: "We hope so."
What previous statements were made about preparations for the exchange
At the end of August, Budanov had already reported that Ukraine was preparing for a new major prisoner exchange. At the time, he noted that contacts with the Russian side mainly concerned the return of people from captivity. At the same time, in his current comment, the head of the Office of the President did not clarify whether the expected exchange was connected with the preparations he had mentioned earlier.
Whom Ukraine returned during the previous stages
According to the Coordination Headquarters for the Treatment of Prisoners of War, on August 19, 2026, as part of the first stage of the latest exchange, 103 Ukrainian servicemen were liberated from Russian captivity. Most of them had injuries and serious illnesses. Those released included representatives of the Armed Forces of Ukraine, the Ukrainian Navy, the Territorial Defense Forces, the National Guard, and the State Border Guard Service. Soldiers, sergeants, and officers returned home. At the time, the Coordination Headquarters expressed gratitude to the United States and the United Arab Emirates for their assistance in organizing the exchange.
The second stage took place on August 24, Ukraine's Independence Day. Another ten Ukrainian servicemen—representatives of the Armed Forces of Ukraine and the National Guard—were returned from the territory of Belarus. A distinctive feature of this stage was that all ten had previously been listed as missing. They had defended Ukraine in the Donetsk sector. Two had been considered missing since 2024, and another eight since 2025.
Nearly 9,700 citizens returned
A September 7 report by the Main Directorate of Intelligence, citing the Chief of the Main Directorate of Intelligence and head of the Coordination Headquarters, Oleh Ivashchenko, stated that 9,726 Ukrainian citizens had been returned home through 77 exchanges and other liberation efforts. This figure includes the results of both exchanges and other operations to return Ukrainians from captivity.
The Coordination Headquarters explains that, during work on exchanges, it considers both servicemen whose presence in captivity has been confirmed and those considered missing. Information about them is collected and updated in the relevant information system.
The Coordination Headquarters does not disclose lists of prisoners and those released for security reasons. Families receive notification that their loved one has been returned by phone, via SMS, and in the "Diia" application.

They added that nearby residents had been evacuated from their homes.

“A number of properties are currently being evacuated in the Whelford area following the declaration of a major incident. It follows the arrest of several men on suspicion of offences under the Explosives Act,” Gloucestershire police said in a statement, referring to a village near the airbase. “The army’s specialist explosive ordnance disposal team is currently examining a number of vehicles.”
The police said they believe the incident was now contained.
The British government said Prime Minister Andy Burnham is being updated about the incident, and it would be inappropriate to comment further while investigations are ongoing.
A spokesperson for the US Air Force declined to discuss specific force protection measures.
“The 501st Combat Support Wing and our fellow UK-based Wings remain vigilant and will take appropriate actions to ensure the safety and security of our US service members, civilians, contractors and their families,” the spokesperson said.
“We constantly assess a variety of factors that determine what measures we institute or modify to protect our installations, our people and their families.”

Hezbollah supporters mark 2 years since Nasrallah’s killing as calls for revenge persist
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-27
07:11:44 UTC
16:11:44 KST

Hezbollah supporters gathered in Lebanon overnight and into Sunday to mark two years since the killing of the terrorist group’s longtime leader Hassan Nasrallah in an Israeli airstrike, as the Iran-backed group confronts continued Israeli attacks and growing domestic pressure over the prospect of renewed war.
Nasrallah was killed Sept. 27, 2024, when the Israeli Air Force struck Hezbollah’s underground headquarters in Haret Hreik, in Beirut’s southern Dahieh district. Supporters gathered overnight at the site of the former command center to commemorate the anniversary of his death.
Shiite supporters also gathered in Baghdad, Iraq, where participants held portraits of Nasrallah to mark two years since his killing.
The Beirut site, once Hezbollah’s central headquarters, was left devastated by the Israeli strike and subsequently became a pilgrimage site for Nasrallah’s supporters. Hezbollah flags and portraits of the slain arch-terrorist have been placed among the ruins, alongside images of Hashem Safieddine, the head of Hezbollah’s Executive Council who had been widely seen as a potential successor to Nasrallah.
Safieddine was himself killed in an Israeli airstrike in October 2024, weeks after Nasrallah’s death.
Additional commemorations were scheduled Sunday at Safieddine’s burial site in the southern Lebanese village of Deir Qanoun al-Nahr, where a ceremony was planned to mark the second anniversary of the deaths of Nasrallah and his would-be successor. Another rally was scheduled at Nasrallah’s burial site along the airport road in Beirut’s southern suburbs.
Nasrallah was killed in a massive Israeli strike on Hezbollah’s underground command headquarters while other senior officials were also inside. According to the IDF, more than 80 bombs were dropped on the bunker as part of an operation dubbed “New Order.”
Ali Karaki, the commander of Hezbollah’s southern front, and other senior members of the group were also killed in the attack.
The anniversary comes as Hezbollah continues to grapple with the consequences of the 2024 war with Israel and debate over its future strategy.
Ibrahim al-Amin, editor of the Lebanese newspaper Al-Akhbar, which is closely associated with Hezbollah, addressed Nasrallah’s killing and the issue of retaliation in an article published Saturday.
“Revenge is a comprehensive mission, founded on absolute belief in its justice and on determination to achieve the best possible results,” al-Amin wrote.
He said retaliation would require a level of sophistication surpassing what he described as Israeli plotting and suggested that carrying it out could become the task of a new generation.
“The appropriate punishment for this state, its government, its people and its institutions is not something ordinary, but a major event that will ensure history remembers it as the clearest expression of justice,” he wrote.
The Qatari-owned newspaper The New Arab, meanwhile, described Hezbollah as facing a difficult strategic position, caught between Israeli military pressure and growing concerns within Lebanon about another conflict.
“Hezbollah today faces a complex and challenging situation,” the newspaper wrote, pointing to continuing Israeli strikes despite a ceasefire agreement, Israel’s presence in parts of southern Lebanon and the continued dismantling and destruction of Hezbollah military infrastructure.
The newspaper said Hezbollah had yet to decide whether to respond and was also facing substantial pressure at home, including opposition from within Lebanon’s Shiite community to actions that could drag the country into another war.
Ghaleb Abu Zeinab, a member of Hezbollah’s Political Council, told The New Arab that September 2024 represented a decisive turning point for the organization.
“We see September 2024 as a crucial turning point. Hezbollah and the resistance are not what they were before,” Abu Zeinab said. “That month marked a significant stage in the conflict with the Israeli enemy.”
He acknowledged that Israel had achieved significant gains through the blows it dealt Hezbollah but said the group did not consider the confrontation over.
“We see the situation with the understanding that the battle with the enemy is still continuing and its end is unknown,” he said. “They may strike us in one place and we may strike them somewhere else, but this is not the end of the road, as the Israelis had hoped it would be.”
Abu Zeinab also rejected the prospect that the existing framework agreement between Lebanon and Israel would produce a lasting settlement.
“We believe the framework agreement that Lebanon signed with Israel will not lead to a real settlement,” he said. “It is unfair and gives Israel an advantage in every one of its provisions. Under no circumstances will we allow Lebanon to be left as easy prey for the enemy.”

What Germany’s Wingcopter 262 Means for Ukraine’s Drone War
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-27
07:11:00 UTC
16:11:00 KST

For years, the German startup Wingcopter built its reputation on civilian logistics. The company engineered autonomous aircraft to deliver life-saving vaccines and medical supplies to isolated communities in Africa and the Pacific. Today, it is making a direct jump into the military sector.
On Sept. 14 Wingcopter unveiled the Wingcopter 262, an all-electric tactical reconnaissance drone equipped with AI. Through a joint venture with Ukrainian manufacturer TAF Industries, these drones are headed straight to the front lines.
JOIN US ON TELEGRAM
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
                                                                                                                                                                         
The move marks two critical developments in the war: commercial tech companies repurposing their civilian tools for military use, and European allies moving Ukrainian defense manufacturing into NATO territory to protect factories from Russian airstrikes.
Hybrid design
The Wingcopter 262 fills a vital tactical gap for Ukrainian forces. It uses a tilt-rotor design, meaning it can take off and land vertically in tight spaces just like a helicopter, but once airborne, it tilts its motors to fly fast and efficiently like a traditional airplane.
This design gets rid of the need for long runways or heavy catapult launchers. A single soldier can carry the 10-kilogram drone into rugged terrain and launch it in just a few minutes.
Zelensky Says Putin Keeps Finding Excuses to Continue the War
Once in the air, the drone can cover a tactical range of 150 kilometers and stay aloft for up to six hours. It carries high-resolution visual and thermal cameras backed by built-in AI, which helps operators spot targets, track movements and process imagery instantly.
Beating signal jamming
One of the drone’s biggest selling points for the front line is its ability to operate when GPS signals are completely cut off.
                                                                                                                                                                         
Russian electronic warfare units continuously flood the front lines with heavy jamming signals. Standard commercial drones that rely entirely on satellite navigation often lose control, drift off course, or crash the moment they hit a jammed sector. Wingcopter built the 262’s navigation system to stay on course even when GPS is blocked, using software fixes shaped directly by feedback from combat operations in Ukraine.
The German-Ukrainian deal
The partnership behind the drone represents a new approach to European defense. Wingcopter and TAF Industries, Ukraine’s largest drone producer, launched a joint venture under the “Build with Ukraine” initiative.
This arrangement fixes a major security issue for Kyiv. Domestic military factories inside Ukraine face constant threats from Russian long-range missile and drone attacks. By partnering with Wingcopter, TAF Industries can mass-produce its battle-tested designs inside secure facilities in Germany. In return, Ukrainian troops get priority access to the new Wingcopter 262 platform.
This partnership creates a shared defense pipeline, which is Ukrainian battle experience combined with German manufacturing power and funding.
Commercial tech reshaping defense
The Wingcopter 262 shows how fast commercial technology can adapt to battlefield realities. The engineering needed to deliver emergency medical packages in harsh weather over long distances turns out to be almost identical to what a military drone needs, with long battery life, reliable navigation and tough airframes that resist signal interference.
As European countries increase their defense spending, military procurement teams are turning away from slow-moving traditional defense contractors. Building a new military aircraft from scratch often takes years. Commercial startups like Wingcopter, which have spent a decade perfecting light electric flight and autonomous software, can deliver proven systems in a fraction of that time.
A high-stakes test for NATO’s future
The deployment of the Wingcopter 262 in Ukraine will act as a real-world stress test. If the aircraft holds up against Russian air defenses and electronic warfare, it will likely capture the attention of other NATO militaries looking to upgrade their tactical reconnaissance gear.
More importantly, the partnership between Wingcopter and TAF Industries proves that it is by moving past one-off weapon donations and fully linking Ukrainian tech into the broader European defense industry, that Western nations can sustain Ukraine over the long haul.

Asian Games | China's 15-year-old Zhu wins women's skateboarding street gold
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-27
15:10:30 CST
16:10:30 KST

Zhu Yuanling of China competes during the women's street final of skateboarding at the 20th Asian Games Aichi-Nagoya 2026 in Tokoname of Aichi Prefecture, Japan, Sept. 27, 2026. (Xinhua/Long Lei)
NAGOYA, Japan, Sept. 27 (Xinhua) -- Fifteen-year-old Zhu Yuanling of China climbed from fifth in qualifying to win the women's skateboarding street gold with 166.57 points at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games on Sunday.
Japan's Yumeka Oda took silver with 161.96, while China's Hangzhou Asian Games champion Cui Chenxi earned bronze. World No. 1 Ibuki Matsumoto of Japan finished fifth.
The street final combines each rider's best of three runs and best of three trick attempts for a total score. Zhu posted two 70-plus run scores and led the field after a third run of 79.73.
In the trick phase, top qualifier Oda opened with 90.75 points, the highest single trick score of the competition, briefly moving into first.
Zhu responded with 78.96 and then landed an 86.84 on her second trick attempt, bringing her total to 166.57 and reclaiming the lead she held until the end.
"I'd been practicing that trick in my second run for a long time, and it's one I can usually land, so I didn't feel like I needed to be that nervous," Zhu said. "It's amazing. I still feel a bit dazed. Actually I didn't expect to win gold."
Cui rose from fourth after the run phase to secure bronze with a standout trick performance.
"I didn't expect to land that trick on the first try, since I hadn't even attempted it before the competition," she said. "Once I landed it, I just went with the flow." ■

Two mass shootings in South Africa at once: 17 people killed in a bar and 10 in a store
Kyiv • UNN
Twenty-seven people were killed in a bar and a store near Johannesburg and Cape Town. The attackers have not yet been apprehended; police are searching for them.
On Sunday, police reported that at least 27 people had been killed in two separate mass shootings near South Africa’s two largest cities, UNN reports, citing AP.
South African police said that 17 people were killed in the early hours of Saturday when attackers armed with AK-47s and pistols opened fire in a bar in the township of Vedela, southwest of Johannesburg.
In another statement, police said that 10 more people were killed during a mass shooting at a shop in the Lwandle area near Cape Town; the incident occurred at around 1 a.m. on Sunday.
The two shootings occurred just days after a mass killing at a house party near the city of Durban on the east coast, where 11 people were killed, including a pregnant woman.
According to police, no one has yet been arrested in connection with the two latest incidents; preliminary information indicates that law enforcement officers are searching for several attackers in both cases.

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday recalled the 2016 surgical strikes carried out by the Indian Army across the Line of Control (LoC), saying India has made it clear that terrorism will be met with a “strong and decisive response”.Addressing the 138th episode of his monthly radio programme Mann Ki Baat, PM Modi said the surgical strikes, carried out on September 28-29, 2016, demonstrated India's resolve to respond to cross-border terrorism.“A major historical achievement of India is set to complete 10 years in just a day—the surgical strike. Ten years ago, on September 28–29, 2016, the Indian Army conducted a surgical strike on terrorist hideouts in PoJK. The world was astonished by the manner in which our brave soldiers crossed the Line of Control (LoC) to take action against terrorism,” he said.PM Modi said the operation had demonstrated a new approach to India's counter-terrorism policy.“The surgical strike boldly demonstrated a new example of India's counter-terrorism policy to the entire world. It served as our decisive response to the long-standing suffering India had endured due to terrorist attacks,” he said.
“India has made it clear that terrorism will be met with a strong and decisive response,” PM Modi added.The Prime Minister also referred to the Balakot airstrike and Operation Sindoor, saying India had repeatedly sent the same message in response to terrorism.“Over the past decade, from the Balakot airstrike to 'Operation Sindoor', India has repeatedly sent a clear message: if terrorists dare to cast a hostile eye on India, they will face a befitting response,” he said.PM Modi also asserted that India was following a policy of “zero tolerance against terrorism”.The surgical strikes were carried out in response to the 2016 Uri terror attack, with the Indian Army targeting terror launch pads across the LoC.
Other highlights from Mann Ki Baat
The Prime Minister also referred to the ongoing Census exercise, describing it as a “national responsibility” and saying every citizen had a role to play. He said the first phase of the Census was almost complete across all states and Union territories, with information on more than 32 crore families already recorded. He urged people to actively participate in the exercise and make use of the online enumeration facility.With October 2 approaching, PM Modi also highlighted cleanliness initiatives being carried out by communities across the country and recalled Mahatma Gandhi's emphasis on cleanliness.“October 2nd is just a few days away; it is the birth anniversary of Revered Bapu. Bapu gave us many mantras for life; cleanliness is one of them,” he said.PM Modi cited examples of youngsters cleaning a river in Madhya Pradesh, restoring old stepwells and wells in Andhra Pradesh, volunteers cleaning Mumbai beaches and young people in Delhi spreading awareness about waste segregation. He also mentioned students and local residents in West Bengal who were cleaning picnic spots.“One thing is clearly evident in all these efforts: it started with one person, then others joined in and the caravan grew. This is public participation,” PM Modi said.“Cleanliness is also the most beautiful tribute we can pay to Bapu,” he added.PM Modi also spoke about the fight against narcotics and said young people were coming together to spread awareness against drug addiction through the Nasha Mukt Yuva Abhiyan. He said millions of young people had taken a pledge to stay away from drugs and had also taken responsibility for spreading the message among others.
The Prime Minister also recalled the history of the Somnath temple, saying those who sought to erase India's identity by destroying it ultimately had no existence. He said the temple continued to stand in its grandeur by the sea, blessing India with immortality.During the broadcast, PM Modi also paid tribute to late VHP leader Ashok Singhal on his birth anniversary, recalling his contribution to the Ram Janmabhoomi movement and describing his life as that of an ascetic who remained engaged with society.

Australia summons OpenAI and Anthropic CEOs to appear at AI inquiry
Call to face Senate inquiry follows security breach of Australia’s Medicare portal by rogue OpenAI bot in June.
Australia has called for the CEOs of OpenAI and Anthropic to appear before a Senate inquiry into artificial intelligence, just days after revelations that a rogue OpenAI bot had hacked the country’s health-system database.
OpenAI’s Sam Altman and Anthropic’s Dario Amodei have been sent written requests to appear at the inquiry, which is to hold public hearings in the capital, Canberra, on Thursday, a spokesperson for Senator Sarah Hanson-Young of the Australian Greens party said.
Recommended Stories
list of 3 items
